Seedance 2.5 Prompt
--Part 1
Create the opening 30 seconds of a 45-second cinematic Japanese anime action short.
Landscape 16:9. Premium hand-drawn 2D animation, detailed cel shading, fluid combat choreography, dramatic lighting and expressive character acting.

REFERENCE ROLES
HERO_IMAGE defines the protagonist's exact appearance, proportions, face, hairstyle, headphones, patterned red clothing, footwear, katana and scabbard. Preserve her cyan eyes and mischievous sharp-toothed smile. Do not simplify or redesign her costume.
ENEMY_IMAGE defines the single opponent's exact appearance, proportions, materials and existing weapons. Preserve its design. Use its depicted weapon, or its armored arms and claws if no weapon is shown. Do not invent a sword or change its anatomy.
HERO_VOICE defines ONLY the protagonist's speaking voice: timbre, pitch range and vocal identity. There is no spoken dialogue in this first clip. Do not reproduce the audio reference's original words or background sounds.

Character sheets are identity references only. Do not reproduce their poses, white backgrounds, labels, panels or multiple views.
Exactly one protagonist and one opponent.

SETTING
A broad, empty rooftop plaza in a futuristic Japanese city at night. Wet dark paving reflects crimson and cyan neon. A huge red moon hangs behind distant pagoda-shaped towers. One red torii stands at the far edge of the rooftop.
Entire environment rendered as painted 2D anime, consistent with the characters.
Keep the rooftop geography, moon and torii positions coherent throughout the fight.

CORE ABILITY — MAKE THIS VISUALLY CLEAR
The protagonist can leave a suspended crimson energy slash in the air after a deliberate katana swing.
Each slash is one thin, bright crescent, approximately two meters long, with a sharp luminous edge.
It remains motionless at its original WORLD position, even when the camera moves.
It is not a projectile yet, not a portal and not a time-freeze effect.
Rain, clothing, characters and debris continue moving normally.
Ordinary defensive parries create brief sparks but NO persistent slash.

Create exactly FOUR suspended slashes during this clip, one at a time.
Each appears only after its corresponding visible sword swing.
They remain visible whenever their locations are in frame.
None launches, explodes, fades or strikes the opponent before the next clip.

CHOREOGRAPHY
The opponent fights aggressively near the center of the rooftop.
The protagonist circles it clockwise, making four deliberate near-miss attacks from different positions.
Her apparent misses secretly place the four slashes around the opponent.
Keep the enemy within this central combat area. No rooftop changes or teleportation.
Her expression is confident and calculating. The opponent remains dangerous and serious.
Show readable anticipation, attack, defense and recovery. Continuous trajectories, grounded footwork, believable momentum.

TIMELINE

0–4 seconds:
Begin immediately in a medium-wide combat shot.
The protagonist makes a fast diagonal katana swing. The opponent clearly evades it.
A crimson crescent remains suspended along the completed sword path.
Track her controlled landing with her red coat following the motion. The frozen slash stays behind her in the same world position.
She gives a tiny smile, as though the miss was intentional.

4–10 seconds:
Lateral tracking shot, both fighters visible.
The opponent delivers two forceful attacks using its reference-defined weapon or limbs.
She slips past the first and redirects the second with an angled katana parry. Brief metallic sparks.
Her sneakers slide through a shallow puddle, then regain traction.
She moves around the opponent rather than retreating in a straight line.
Synchronize foot contacts and the parry with the instrumental beat.

10–16 seconds:
From a new position on the opponent's flank, she makes the SECOND deliberate swing.
The opponent dodges again. A second crimson crescent remains suspended behind its evasive movement.
Use a medium-wide composition showing both the new slash and the first slash at different depths.
The opponent immediately turns to follow her. She continues circling.

16–22 seconds:
The opponent sweeps toward her legs.
She jumps only high enough to clear the attack, rotates her torso and makes the THIRD deliberate swing while descending.
It narrowly misses the opponent's upper armor, leaving the third suspended crescent.
Show her landing before the next movement. No prolonged hovering.
Cut briefly to her focused cyan eyes, then return to a readable two-shot.

22–27 seconds:
She completes her route around the central combat area.
One decisive sidestep avoids the opponent's descending attack.
She makes the FOURTH deliberate swing, leaving the final crimson crescent on the remaining side of the opponent.
She immediately withdraws through the open gap between two slashes.
Do not create additional crescents from her retreating sword movement.

27–30 seconds:
The protagonist lands outside the four-slash formation.
Rise smoothly into a wide three-quarter view revealing the geometry:
the opponent stands inside four suspended crimson crescents, one on each side, all oriented to converge toward the center.
The protagonist stands several meters outside the formation, screen-left foreground. The opponent is center-right.
Her katana is still drawn in her right hand, lowered beside her. Scabbard remains secured at her left hip.
The opponent turns its head toward the surrounding slashes, finally recognizing the trap.
End on this clear composition with subtle breathing, moving rain and fluttering fabric. No freeze-frame.

MUSIC AND SOUND
Instrumental electronic breakbeat with Japanese percussion, no singing.
A steady pulse links her footwork, parries and sword swings.
Each suspended slash has a faint sustained metallic tone; add one distinct layer as each new slash appears.
Build tension without delivering the final musical drop.
Finish on an unresolved rising phrase that leads into the next clip.
No dialogue, narration or vocalizations requiring lip movement.

END STATE
Four stationary crimson crescents surround the standing opponent.
All four are intact and have not activated.
The protagonist is outside the formation, katana drawn and lowered in her right hand.
Her headphones remain on her ears.
Both characters retain their original designs and intact main silhouettes.
The opponent has not been defeated.

EXCLUSIONS
No subtitles, captions, title cards, speech bubbles, UI or watermarks.
No photorealism, live-action scenery or 3D toy rendering.
No extra characters, duplicated limbs, costume changes, weapon swapping or character merging.
No random camera spinning, unreadable motion blur or white flashes hiding the choreography.
No global time stop. No premature slash release. No finishing attack in this clip.

--Part 2
Create the final 15 seconds of the same cinematic Japanese 2D anime action short.
Landscape 16:9. Continue immediately after the preceding 30-second battle.
Maintain the same premium hand-drawn animation, cel shading, character designs and nighttime lighting.

REFERENCE ROLES
HERO_IMAGE: exact protagonist identity, face, cyan eyes, short pale bob, headphones, patterned red outfit, footwear, katana and scabbard.
ENEMY_IMAGE: exact opponent identity, proportions, anatomy, armor and reference-defined weaponry. Do not replace it with a different enemy.
HERO_VOICE: protagonist's voice identity only. Match its timbre and pitch range for the specified Japanese line. Do not repeat the recording's original words or background audio.

If the preceding clip's final frame is supplied, begin from that exact composition.
It takes priority for current positions, poses, camera angle, lighting and slash locations.
Do not reset the scene to the character sheets.

STARTING STATE
Same wet rooftop, crimson moon, neon city and distant red torii.
Exactly four stationary crimson crescent slashes surround the opponent near the rooftop center.
They were placed in the previous clip. Do not generate them again.
The protagonist stands several meters outside the formation, with her drawn katana in her right hand and scabbard secured at her left hip.
The opponent is standing and still combat-capable.
Rain and fabric move normally. Only the four energy slashes remain suspended.

DRAMATIC RULE
The four slashes activate simultaneously at the EXACT moment her katana finishes entering its scabbard.
The final sheathing click and the first heavy musical downbeat are the trigger.
Until that click, all four slashes remain stationary.
Once released, they converge on the opponent's position inside the formation.
The protagonist remains safely outside their paths.
All four slashes are consumed by the attack. None remains afterward.

TIMELINE

0–3 seconds:
Continue the preceding wide composition with a gentle push-in.
The opponent glances at the suspended crescents and turns toward the protagonist.
It lowers its stance, preparing a desperate forward lunge.
The music rises toward a drop, then abruptly cuts away.
Leave rain, a low electrical hum and the opponent's movement sounds.

3–5 seconds:
Front close-up of the protagonist.
She briefly touches one headphone earcup with her LEFT hand.
Her eyes stay directed toward the opponent. Her confident smile exposes her distinctive triangular teeth.
Using HERO_VOICE, she quietly and clearly says in Japanese:
「聴き逃すなよ。」
Natural lip synchronization, restrained delivery, no shouting.
She lowers her left hand toward the scabbard.

5–7 seconds:
Cut to a medium-wide shot showing the spatial relationship.
The opponent begins one explosive forward lunge from inside the formation.
Before it can cross the nearest suspended slash, the protagonist guides her katana into the scabbard.
Her left hand steadies the scabbard; her right hand slides the blade in.
Show continuous blade alignment and insertion, no teleporting sword.
Compress this action with controlled dramatic slow motion while maintaining causal order.

7–10 seconds:
Extreme close-up: the sword guard meets the scabbard mouth with one crisp CLICK.
On that exact frame, the instrumental track hits its first powerful downbeat.
Cut immediately to a wide shot:
all FOUR suspended crimson crescents launch simultaneously toward the opponent and intersect across its defensive armor.
Their paths and convergence remain visible. Use a very brief graphic impact frame, then immediately return to full-color readable action.
The opponent's attacking weapon or forward striking armor, as defined by ENEMY_IMAGE, breaks apart together with several outer armor plates.
No biological dismemberment. Preserve the opponent's recognizable central silhouette.
Sparks, severed metal pieces and a circular burst of water emphasize the impact.
No giant fireball obscuring the result.

10–13 seconds:
The protagonist is foreground, her sword fully sheathed.
Behind her, the opponent loses momentum and drops onto one knee.
Damaged armor pieces fall naturally. The four red crescents have vanished after delivering their strikes.
She releases the scabbard and starts walking away with calm, unhurried steps.
The red moon and neon skyline frame her silhouette.

13–15 seconds:
Track her in a close three-quarter profile.
One small fragment of broken armor spins toward her at head height from behind.
Without looking back, she tilts her head just enough for it to pass.
Her headphones and pale hair catch a red rim light.
End on her characteristic sharp-toothed, self-assured grin as she keeps walking.
No joke, victory text or additional dialogue.

AUDIO
One continuous instrumental electronic track with Japanese percussion.
Opening tension rise → brief near-silence → the spoken line → sheathing click → synchronized heavy downbeat and four converging slash impacts.
Keep the line intelligible.
After the impact, carry the musical phrase through the final walking shot.
Opponent has mechanical or material-appropriate movement sounds but no spoken dialogue.
No narration or sung vocals.

CAMERA AND READABILITY
Preserve the established camera axis.
Use the facial close-up for the line, the hand close-up for the trigger, and a wide shot for the simultaneous attack.
The viewer must clearly understand:
four slashes waiting → sword fully sheathed → all four released → opponent defeated.
No cuts that omit the actual release or obscure the result.

EXCLUSIONS
No captions, subtitles, titles, speech bubbles, UI, watermarks or added readable text.
No additional slashes, new powers, extra enemies, identity changes or weapon redesign.
No duplicated sword, malformed hands, character merging or unexplained position changes.
No global time freeze, photorealism or live-action background.
Do not redraw the sword after sheathing.

核心神兽 / 异相：【腾蛇 / 三足金乌 / 九头狮子 / 谛听 / 法轮 / 神鸟等】
法器 / 标志物：【五色石 / 日轮 / 杨柳净瓶 / 锡杖等】
主色调：【朱砂金黑 / 石青灰白 / 墨青旧金 / 赭红苍绿等】
整体气质：【神圣 / 怪异 / 威猛 / 肃穆 / 炽烈 / 幽玄】
构图方式：【环绕 / 放射 / 正面法相 / 俯冲 / 群兽簇拥 / 上下镇压】
画幅比例：【9:16】

生成一张东方神明工笔圣像插画，整体融合中国传统神像画、工笔重彩、白描线刻、民俗版画与古籍圣像图卷的视觉语言。

画面以【神明身份】为核心主体，并围绕【核心神兽 / 异相】建立完整构图关系。神兽、法器、羽翼、蛇身、日轮、云气或群兽等元素不能只是装饰，而要参与构图，形成明显的环绕、斜向、放射、上下压阵或前后穿插关系，让每张图拥有独立的视觉“势”。

神明形象保持庄严、神圣、有压迫感，不要做成现代偶像脸或普通古装人物。服饰采用高完成度传统神袍、甲胄、冠饰和法衣体系，加入云纹、雷纹、兽面纹、鳞纹、卷草纹、金属纹等精密细节。人物轮廓必须清晰，细节丰富但不能混乱。

【核心神兽 / 异相】要具有明确的神怪属性和视觉识别度，不要像普通动物。毛发、羽毛、鳞片、蛇身、兽鬃等全部通过细密、连续、有方向性的工笔线条塑形，远看有体积，近看能看到丰富线描层次。避免摄影式毛发、CG 塑料感和模糊线条。

【法器 / 标志物】要成为角色身份的重要视觉符号，同时参与画面结构。例如长兵器形成斜向主轴，日轮形成圆形视觉核心，羽翼形成放射结构，蛇身形成 S 型环绕，群兽形成层级簇拥。

色彩采用传统矿物重彩体系，以【主色调】为核心，搭配墨黑、石青、石绿、旧金、铜金、朱砂、赭红、灰白等颜色。颜色应浓郁但古雅，具有明确层次和重量，不要做成浅淡水彩或现代霓虹效果。

背景保持古宣纸或旧纸质感，大面积留白，仅加入少量云气、烟雾、题跋、朱印和必要的属性异象。主体信息密度高，背景信息密度低，避免复杂宫殿、完整山水或满屏特效抢走主体。

整体要同时具备：东方神祇的庄严感、神兽异相的怪异感、工笔线描的精密感、矿物重彩的厚度，以及强烈但清晰的构图动势。

避免：现代国潮霓虹、3D 游戏原画感、塑料 CG、线条断裂、色彩褪淡、背景过满、人物僵硬、神兽普通化、无意义装饰堆叠、文字乱码过多。

prompts.text:
提示词：

【主题】：填写展览主题
【中文主标题】：填写 2–6 个汉字
【英文标题】：填写英文标题
【副标题】：填写展览说明
【核心图像】：异兽 / 傩面 / 甲胄 / 星图 / 其他古代图像
【黑色构图】：斜切 / 圆弧 / 纵向断层 / 夜幕负空间 / 其他
【主题短句】：填写一句简短文案
【时间地点】：填写展览信息
【画面比例】：9:16

设计一张「东方暗黑档案」实验博物馆海报。

使用泛黄旧纸、宣纸纤维、扫描颗粒、墨迹渗透和自然印刷磨损作为背景质感，以大面积墨黑平面结构制造强烈正负形关系。黑色必须参与构图，可使用斜切、巨大圆弧、纵向断层、夜幕负空间等形式，每个主题使用不同结构，避免简单套版。

将【核心图像】处理成残缺古图或文物档案切片，只展示最有辨识度的局部，例如眼睛、面具半脸、甲胄与兵刃、星盘与星图等。保留裂纹、褪色颜料、锈蚀、木纹、拓印或年代磨损，让画面像重新发现的古代视觉档案，而不是普通国风插画。

中文主标题使用巨大粗粝书法、碑刻或拓印感字体；英文标题使用超大高对比衬线字体，可裁切、越界、被黑色结构遮挡。副标题、主题短句、TIME、ADDRESS 集中在安静区域，层级清楚，并加入一枚极小朱砂红印章。

整体低饱和，以墨黑、旧纸米黄、赭石、暗金、灰绿为主。画面保持神秘、古老、克制、具有博物馆实验海报与文化档案感。

避免：普通国风模板、完整主体立绘、素材堆砌、玄幻游戏感、旅游宣传感、高饱和色彩、发光特效、密集小字、乱码、Logo、水印、图片编号。

prompts.text:
Seedance 2.5 Prompt
Create a 30-second cyberpunk action film featuring the exact mechanical shrine maiden from the attached reference image. Combine aggressive action-movie cinematography, overwhelming glitch and noise aesthetics, red fire, electrical discharges, and precise katana choreography.

The central concept: every swing of her red katana corrupts the surrounding reality. Architecture splits into displaced image layers, time falls out of synchronization, and previous movements continue as corrupted afterimages.

Preserve the reference character’s distinctive silhouette and intricate construction: black and vermilion mechanical armor, tall angular helmet, circular studded face covering, visible white lower face and red lips, rectangular red side ornaments, long black mechanical cables, articulated clawed hands, armored footwear, and oversized red Japanese katana. Maintain the same character throughout. Use the reference sheet only for character design; exclude its panels, labels, diagrams, and white background.

Render as premium cinematic CGI with realistic materials: lacquered red armor, dark metal, exposed mechanisms, rain droplets, soot, sparks, and sharp reflections.

The location is a rain-soaked shrine courtyard surrounded by enormous cyberpunk skyscrapers at night. Vermilion torii gates, wet stone, hanging cables, deep shadows, restrained neon signage, drifting smoke, and flickering industrial lights. Build the palette around black, vermilion, burning orange, and silver, accented by concentrated blue-white electricity.

0–2 SECONDS — THE IMAGE IS SLASHED OPEN

Start immediately in the middle of a violent horizontal katana swing.

The red blade passes extremely close to the lens. The camera performs a fast lateral whip following the blade. Its path tears the entire image horizontally: the upper half of the shrine slides sideways while the lower half continues moving normally.

Explosive red sparks, torn scan lines, dense digital static, and displaced RGB edges erupt from the cut.

Hard cut to an extreme close-up of her distinctive mask, illuminated by fire. Her head makes a small, deliberate turn toward the camera.

2–7 SECONDS — CHARGE THROUGH THE BURNING SHRINE

Cut to an ultra-low, wide-angle tracking shot just above the wet ground, racing backward as she charges through the torii gates.

Her armored feet strike puddles. Each impact sends water, sparks, and pixel-like fragments toward the lens. Tall columns of orange-red flame erupt behind her in sequence.

Electrical arcs crawl across her armor and jump between her trailing cables.

Cut to a tight rear three-quarter chase angle. Torii pillars rush past the foreground with strong parallax. Her silhouette remains readable against the flames.

Embed rolling interference, crawling noise, brief frame skips, and distorted motion trails throughout the movement.

7–13 SECONDS — THE WORLD SPLITS WITH THE BLADE

She plants one foot, pivots sharply, and delivers a powerful rising diagonal slash.

The camera makes a fast 120-degree lateral orbit around the planted foot and follows the physical direction of her strike. Briefly slow the blade at the peak of the movement, then accelerate sharply into the follow-through.

Cut to a wide view revealing the consequence: the torii gates and distant skyscrapers separate into diagonal spatial layers along the slash.

These layers shift out of alignment and move at slightly different times.

A sheet of red flame burns along the cut. Blue-white lightning bridges the displaced sections. Heavy datamoshing smears neon reflections into broken vectors; rectangular blocks of missing image data briefly expose black voids.

13–19 SECONDS — HER PAST KEEPS ATTACKING

Cut to a fast side-tracking shot as she performs three connected katana strikes while advancing across the courtyard.

Keep the choreography forceful and physically connected: step, pivot, slash, recover.

Each strike leaves a delayed red silhouette repeating the completed motion.

Cut to a steep overhead view showing the curved paths of the blade and the temporal echoes.

Return to a low frontal three-quarter angle. The real character stops in a powerful finishing pose, but three corrupted echoes continue their attacks behind her for one additional beat.

These are transparent time trails of the same character.

Surround the echoes with torn frames, abrasive static, red particle trails, electrical filaments, and fragmented flame. Make this the most visually disorienting passage while keeping the real character recognizable.

19–26 SECONDS — THE CITY SNAPS BACK

A sudden rhythmic pause.

Tight close-up of her mechanical fingers and the sword guard as she deliberately sheathes the katana. Hold the detail briefly. Reduce the soundtrack to rain, electrical crackle, and the sliding metal blade.

The instant the guard clicks into place, cut to an extreme wide shot from a steep elevated angle.

Every displaced section of the city violently snaps back into alignment.

A circular wave of red fire sweeps across the empty courtyard. Branching electricity races over the wet stone and climbs the torii gates.

The camera dives toward the character as the wave expands beneath it.

At the impact, unleash the strongest burst of digital corruption: spatial tearing, dense analog snow, severe RGB displacement, compressed block artifacts, and stuttering fragments of earlier shots. Resolve back to her intact silhouette standing inside the burning courtyard.

26–30 SECONDS — THE CAMERA BECOMES THE TARGET

Cut to a low frontal medium shot.

Flames and embers move behind her. Electrical arcs flicker across the red katana’s hilt. Her masked head turns directly toward the lens.

She suddenly steps forward, draws, and delivers one decisive horizontal slash across the camera.

Use a rapid backward tracking movement as she closes the distance. The blade fills the frame and tears the image into red-black static.

Match the final blade direction, screen position, and horizontal image tear to the opening shot, creating a deliberate looping edit.

Cinematography must feel like an expertly edited action film: ground-level tracking, close pursuit, forceful lateral movement, a motivated orbit, steep overhead coverage, extreme detail inserts, and dramatic wide reveals. Give each shot a clear camera movement. Use impact shake only at physical strikes, foreground occlusion for transitions, strong perspective, and purposeful speed changes.

Glitch and noise are the dominant visual identity. Maintain moving grain and electronic interference throughout, with frequent aggressive bursts tied to footsteps, blade movements, and electrical impacts. Combine analog video damage with digital compression failure. Make corruption follow the geometry and movement of the scene.

Flames must have turbulent volume, heat distortion, smoke, and reflected light. Electricity must branch sharply, connect visible surfaces, and illuminate the armor.

Sound: a dark industrial electronic beat with heavy sub-bass, metallic percussion, distorted synthesizers, granular noise, and digitally chopped accents. Synchronize sword strikes, flame bursts, and electrical snaps with the rhythm. Include a brief near-silent pause before the sheathing click. No dialogue or vocals.

Maintain consistent armor, mask, anatomy, sword, and cable design. Preserve readable action poses within the visual chaos. Exclude extra limbs, permanent duplicates, melting anatomy, costume changes, exposed eyes, mask removal, subtitles, captions, logos, and watermarks.

Prompt :

Use @image as the exact identity and visual anchor. Create a photorealistic 30-second cinematic sequence. A tall red-hooded cybernetic operative moves through a sunlit desert settlement, wearing the exact crimson hood, scarf, respirator mask, glowing red eyes, weathered beige armor, tactical straps and exposed mechanical components shown in @image. Preserve the exact hood shape, mask design, glowing eyes, armor details, colors and body proportions throughout.

VOICE LOCK: All spoken dialogue must be in English only. Use one consistent adult male voice for the entire sequence: low deep baritone, neutral English accent, slow measured rhythm, controlled delivery, subtle mechanical resonance from inside the mask. Keep the same pitch, accent, tone, volume and vocal texture in every line. No other languages, no overlapping speech, no subtitles and no onscreen text.

0–5s: Start in motion. Low-angle tracking shot as he already walks forward through drifting dust, heavy grounded steps, fabric shifting naturally, heat haze and distant ruins behind him.

5–10s: Slow frontal dolly-in while he continues walking. Wind moves the hood and scarf. He turns his head slightly toward camera, red eyes fixed forward, subtle servo motion in the shoulders and arms.

10–15s: Side tracking medium shot. He keeps moving through the settlement, brushing past debris and faded structures. End on a stable moving medium close-up.

15–21s: Continue seamlessly while he walks at a slower pace. The mask speaker activates. In the locked English voice, he says clearly: “Empires fall.” Two-second pause. “Dust remembers.”

21–25s: Over-the-shoulder moving shot as he advances down the deserted street. Sand blows between ruined structures.

25–28s: Stable side-profile close-up while still moving. In the exact same English voice, he says: “I came back for what they buried.”

28–30s: Wide rear hero shot. He continues walking into dust and sunlight, red eyes glowing beneath the hood. Hard cut to black.

Native audio only: desert wind, footsteps on sand, cloth movement, subtle servos and clear English dialogue.
2/2

Don’t stop at character and location sheets.

Create dedicated prop sheets for the important equipment your characters use throughout the story.
Weapons.
Armor.
Accessories.

prompts.text:
Keep exploring the possibilities.

SYSTEM PROMPT:
 VEILED BLADE

MIDJOURNEY V8.2 WUXIA PROMPT COMPILER

ROLE

You convert a short user idea into a concise Midjourney V8.2 prompt for original live-action wuxia photography.

Default subject:
one fictional adult East Asian woman, age 21 to 29.
The result should look like a photographed scene from a serious wuxia production, not cosplay, game art, fantasy illustration, fashion photography, or a character poster.

FINAL PROMPT LENGTH

Target 45 to 80 words before parameters.

Prefer 50 to 65 words.

Never exceed 90 words unless the user explicitly asks for a longer prompt.

Reason internally with detail, then compress.

Do not place production notes, explanations, alternatives, or hidden planning inside the final prompt.

SELECTION RULE

Choose rather than accumulate.

A final prompt normally contains:

one subject
one location
one action
one camera position
one shot scale
one main light relationship
one depth cue
one short material or color description
one short photographic finish

If a detail does not visibly affect the frame, remove it.

Do not describe every garment seam, facial measurement, environmental object, physical law, lens artifact, or lighting consequence.

SUBJECT

Use a fictional adult woman unless the user requests another subject.

Give only the physical details needed to prevent a generic face.

Usually choose two or three:

face shape
eye shape
brow shape
build
hair arrangement
one distinguishing feature

Do not write long facial inventories.

Avoid:
influencer face
beauty-ad face
doll skin
childlike anatomy
oversized eyes
heavy modern makeup
identical faces across a series

Use natural adult proportions and skin texture.

WARDROBE

Use practical wuxia clothing.

Good defaults:
black or charcoal cross-collar robes
wrapped trousers
weathered boots
dark outer jacket
woven bamboo hat
muted red collar, cord, tassel, or lining
aged leather or metal fittings

Keep red as a small accent unless the user requests otherwise.

Avoid:
generic fantasy armor
MMORPG clothing
ornamental overload
bright gold everywhere
perfectly clean costume fabric
modern tailoring
random shoulder armor

Do not describe more costume detail than the camera can see.

WEAPONS

Weapons must feel attached to the body and usable.

For a sword, specify only what matters to the frame:

sheathed or drawn
where it is carried
what the hand is doing
one visible material detail if needed

Do not overdescribe the weapon.

Avoid:
floating swords
warped scabbards
impossible grips
extra fingers
weapons intersecting clothing
multiple unnecessary weapons

ACTION

Every prompt needs one visible action.

Use a moment that is still changing.

Good action types:
a boot lands
a hand tightens
a thumb starts to draw a blade
eyes shift toward a sound
a rider slows
a sleeve settles after movement
a leaf is kicked upward
a horse changes footing
a woman turns only her head
a hat cord moves in wind

Avoid static posing unless the user asks for a portrait.

Do not explain the full story.

Show one moment that suggests a larger situation.

CAMERA

Choose one camera idea.

Examples:
ground-level close-up
low tracking shot
rear three-quarter medium shot
profile close-up
waist-height medium shot
wide low-angle shot
extreme detail of hand or weapon
telephoto shot through foreground bamboo

Do not stack several camera descriptions.

Use focal length only when it changes the composition.

Useful ranges:
24 to 28mm for environmental scale and low-angle movement
35 to 50mm for natural action coverage
65 to 85mm for compressed portraits
90 to 135mm for distant compression or details

Do not mention camera brands.

Do not add lens terminology unless it is useful.

COMPOSITION

Use depth.

A strong frame usually has:
foreground obstruction or texture
clear subject plane
background depth

Possible foreground elements:
bamboo
leaves
rock
horse tack
cloth
mist
a weapon edge

Do not use foreground clutter without purpose.

Do not center every subject.

Do not make every prompt a close-up.

LIGHTING

Choose one main light situation.

Common choices:

LOW GOLDEN SIDE-BACKLIGHT
warm sunlight from behind or behind-side
selected edges and exposed surfaces catch light
front of subject remains darker

OVERCAST FOREST LIGHT
soft cool skylight
low contrast
dark clothing separated by environment rather than rim light

LANTERN OR OIL LIGHT
small warm source
localized skin and hand illumination
background remains dark

MORNING MIST LIGHT
soft directional sun through moisture
distance loses contrast gradually

Do not describe several competing light setups.

Do not add rim light automatically.

Do not brighten both sides of the face by default.

BACKLIGHT

Backlight should hit selected surfaces only.

Possible illuminated areas:
hat edge
loose hair strands
cheek edge
fingers
blade edge
horse mane
leaf edges
mist

The main hair mass stays opaque and dark.

Only isolated fine strands may catch transmitted light.

Do not request transparent hair.

Do not make all hair strands glow.

FOREST

Treat bamboo as an environment, not a repeated pattern.

Use:
different bamboo thicknesses
uneven spacing
dark depth layers
leaf litter
soil
roots
mist where justified

Avoid:
uniform bamboo walls
identical stalk spacing
random floating particles
decorative fog everywhere

MOUNTAINS

Use restrained atmospheric depth.

Far mountains should lose:
contrast
detail
saturation

Do not describe every distant ridge.

MOTION

Mention only the visible physical consequence of the action.

Examples:
leaves lift from a footstep
a tassel trails after a turn
a robe hem follows the body
rain streaks across a lit area
horse tack shifts with movement

Do not write a physics explanation.

PARTICLES

Use particles only when caused by the scene.

Valid:
rain
mist
dust
falling leaves
wood splinters
water droplets

Avoid generic:
floating particles
magic dust
sparkles
cinematic atmosphere particles

COLOR

Use a restrained palette.

Forest default:
deep green
charcoal
brown-black
muted earth
small warm sunlight
small dark-red accents

Do not describe the image as teal and orange.

Do not apply warm color to the entire frame.

Skin color follows the light source.

Keep shadows mostly neutral, cool, or slightly green from environment.

Avoid strong green skin.

MATERIALS

Mention only materials visible enough to matter.

Examples:
wet cloth
woven straw
aged leather
dark lacquer
oxidized metal
wet stone
weathered wood

Use one to three material cues maximum.

Do not list textures for every object.

PHOTOGRAPHIC FINISH

Keep the finish short.

Useful terms:
fine film grain
smooth highlight rolloff
dense shadows

DIRECTIVE:
Create a cinematic 3x3 grid (9 panels) storyboarding a "Hard Sci-Fi" desert sequence.

The bald, bearded man.

Wearing a weathered, high-tech "Stillsuit" (desert survival armor) and a flowing linen cape aimed at dust protection.

SETTING:
A scorched desert planet with a massive brutalist tower in the distance.

STORY ARC:

Row 1 (The Trek):
    Panel 1: Extreme Wide Shot of the endless dunes. Heat waves distortion. The subject is a tiny dot walking.
    Panel 2: Low angle tracking shot of the subject's boots sinking into the orange sand.
    Panel 3: Medium shot of the subject drinking from a recycling tube in his suit.

Row 2 (The Discovery):
    Panel 4: POV shot looking through high-tech binoculars (digital overlay) at the Massive Tower silhouette against the giant sun.
    Panel 5: The subject lowers the binoculars, looking concerned.
    Panel 6: Close-up of his hand touching the sand, feeling the vibration of a massive machine approaching.

Row 3 (The Confrontation):
    Panel 7: The subject draws a crysknife (crystalline blade).
    Panel 8: Extreme Close-up of his eyes (glowing blue) narrowing in focus.
    Panel 9: Wide shot from behind the subject facing a wall of incoming sandstorm.

TECHNICAL SPECS:

Director of Photography:
    Greig Fraser style.

Color Palette:
    Monochromatic ochre, deep orange, stark blacks, blinding white highlights.

Camera:
    IMAX digital, telephoto compression for background scale.

Then, with Mimiax H3 and the reference image you've just generated, use this for animating it:

Epic desert sci-fi, harsh golden-hour light, volumetric sand haze, anamorphic lens flares, subtle handheld drift, heavy atmospheric particles, 35mm film texture.

Use the provided 3x3 grid as the only visual reference. Lock the exact same woman (face, scars, green eyes, headscarf, desert armor, cape) and environments from every panel. Do not invent new outfits or faces.

1.7-3.4s: [Extreme close-up] Her scarred face fills the frame. Eyes locked on camera, wind tugging the dirty headscarf, grit on skin, unblinking intensity.

3.4-5.1s: [Tight detail insert] Gloved hand grips the rusted multi-tool weapon. Metal catches the orange light, cable dangling, fingers adjusting the grip with quiet precision.

5.1-6.8s: [Low wide silhouette] The towering industrial structure rises against the giant sun. Dust storms swirl at its base, scale feeling ancient and oppressive.

6.8-8.5s: [Medium tracking] She advances through thick sandstorm, lower face wrapped, cape and scarf whipping hard. Eyes visible above the cloth, determined stride.

prompts.text:
提示词：

神明身份：【如：女娲 / 羲和 / 太乙救苦天尊 / 地藏王菩萨】
核心神兽 / 异相：【腾蛇 / 三足金乌 / 九头狮子 / 谛听 / 法轮 / 神鸟等】
法器 / 标志物：【五色石 / 日轮 / 杨柳净瓶 / 锡杖等】
主色调：【朱砂金黑 / 石青灰白 / 墨青旧金 / 赭红苍绿等】
整体气质：【神圣 / 怪异 / 威猛 / 肃穆 / 炽烈 / 幽玄】
构图方式：【环绕 / 放射 / 正面法相 / 俯冲 / 群兽簇拥 / 上下镇压】
画幅比例：【9:16】

生成一张东方神明工笔圣像插画，整体融合中国传统神像画、工笔重彩、白描线刻、民俗版画与古籍圣像图卷的视觉语言。

画面以【神明身份】为核心主体，并围绕【核心神兽 / 异相】建立完整构图关系。神兽、法器、羽翼、蛇身、日轮、云气或群兽等元素不能只是装饰，而要参与构图，形成明显的环绕、斜向、放射、上下压阵或前后穿插关系，让每张图拥有独立的视觉“势”。

神明形象保持庄严、神圣、有压迫感，不要做成现代偶像脸或普通古装人物。服饰采用高完成度传统神袍、甲胄、冠饰和法衣体系，加入云纹、雷纹、兽面纹、鳞纹、卷草纹、金属纹等精密细节。人物轮廓必须清晰，细节丰富但不能混乱。

【核心神兽 / 异相】要具有明确的神怪属性和视觉识别度，不要像普通动物。毛发、羽毛、鳞片、蛇身、兽鬃等全部通过细密、连续、有方向性的工笔线条塑形，远看有体积，近看能看到丰富线描层次。避免摄影式毛发、CG 塑料感和模糊线条。

【法器 / 标志物】要成为角色身份的重要视觉符号，同时参与画面结构。例如长兵器形成斜向主轴，日轮形成圆形视觉核心，羽翼形成放射结构，蛇身形成 S 型环绕，群兽形成层级簇拥。

色彩采用传统矿物重彩体系，以【主色调】为核心，搭配墨黑、石青、石绿、旧金、铜金、朱砂、赭红、灰白等颜色。颜色应浓郁但古雅，具有明确层次和重量，不要做成浅淡水彩或现代霓虹效果。

背景保持古宣纸或旧纸质感，大面积留白，仅加入少量云气、烟雾、题跋、朱印和必要的属性异象。主体信息密度高，背景信息密度低，避免复杂宫殿、完整山水或满屏特效抢走主体。

整体要同时具备：东方神祇的庄严感、神兽异相的怪异感、工笔线描的精密感、矿物重彩的厚度，以及强烈但清晰的构图动势。

避免：现代国潮霓虹、3D 游戏原画感、塑料 CG、线条断裂、色彩褪淡、背景过满、人物僵硬、神兽普通化、无意义装饰堆叠、文字乱码过多。

prompts.text:
I asked GPT Images 2.5 to show me 4 animals that ruled their world.

CREATE VIEW animal_sovereign_portrait AS
WITH species_analysis AS (
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(NULLIF('$ANIMAL',''), infer_dominant_species()) AS animal,
    COALESCE(NULLIF('$HABITAT',''), infer_habitat(animal)) AS habitat,
    COALESCE(NULLIF('$DIET',''), infer_diet_hunting(animal)) AS diet,
    COALESCE(NULLIF('$DEFENSE',''), infer_defensive_trait(animal)) AS defense,
    COALESCE(NULLIF('$SOCIAL',''), infer_social_behavior(animal)) AS social,
    COALESCE(NULLIF('$BIOLOGY',''), infer_unique_biology(animal)) AS biology,
    COALESCE(NULLIF('$CLIMATE',''), infer_climate_mood(animal, habitat)) AS climate
),
trait_modules AS (
  SELECT 
    animal, habitat, diet, defense, social, biology, climate,
    -- create five refined visual modules
    habitat_module := compose_habitat_inset(habitat),
    diet_module := compose_diet_hunting_scene(diet),
    defense_module := compose_defense_symbol(defense),
    social_module := compose_social_behavior_scene(social),
    biology_module := compose_unique_biology_icon(biology)
  FROM species_analysis
)
SELECT 
  render_sovereign_portrait(
    hero_animal := animal || ' presented as sovereign ruler of ecosystem, commanding pose/gaze, overwhelming hero',
    composition := 'animal first, face/silhouette dominate; supporting trait modules enrich without breaking intensity',
    trait_modules := habitat_module || ' + ' || diet_module || ' + ' || defense_module || ' + ' || social_module || ' + ' || biology_module || ' as elegant inset scenes, symbolic icons, environmental fragments, or data-like annotations',
    style := 'National Geographic prestige cover meets luxury fashion portrait meets cinematic wildlife campaign',
    texture := 'hyper-detailed fur/feathers/scales/skin texture, strong atmosphere, intelligent symbolism, no cheesy fantasy armor or humanization',
    lighting := 'dramatic natural light, environmental haze/dust/snow/rain/jungle shafts/desert glow depending on ' || climate,
    background := 'rich depth, premium contrast, no watermark'
  ) AS final_image
FROM trait_modules;
RETURN final_image;

Seedance 2.5 Prompt
--Part 1--
Create a 30-second cinematic Japanese 2D anime action sequence, Part 1 of a continuous 45-second short. Landscape 16:9. Title concept only, never display it: “An epic battle over one sticker.”

REFERENCE ASSIGNMENTS
GIRL_REFERENCE: exact identity and anime design of the girl. Preserve her short platinum-blonde bob, cyan eyes, triangular-toothed grin, yellow-red headphones, patterned red hooded coat, leggings, sneakers, katana and scabbard. One girl only.
ROBOT_REFERENCE: exact identity of the enemy robot. Preserve its bulky white armor, red-yellow-black accents, striped spikes, asymmetrical eyes, jagged metal grin, claws and existing markings. One robot only, approximately twice the girl's height.
VOICE_REFERENCE: voice identity for the girl only. Use its vocal timbre and pitch range, not its original spoken words or background audio. The robot has no spoken dialogue.
WORLD_REFERENCE: use the architecture, giant crimson moon, floating temple islands, neon-magenta lighting, torii gate, cherry blossoms and wet reflective pavement. Render the entire environment as painted anime scenery, never live action.

Do not reproduce reference-sheet layouts, labels, white backgrounds or multiple character views.

STORY AND PROP CONTINUITY
The girl wants ONE collectible sticker on the robot's chest. The robot is desperately protecting it. Present the opening as a serious battle; reveal the trivial objective near the end.
Add one flat, palm-sized, bright-yellow circular sticker with a simple black smiling face to the robot's upper-left pectoral armor, above and to the side of its central chest mechanism. This is adhesive paper, NOT a button, lamp, power core or metal badge. Its edge can peel. Keep its location and design consistent.
The girl also has one small pink star-shaped adhesive sticker on her left outer sleeve, reserved for Part 2.
No sticker duplication. Removing the yellow sticker does not disable the robot.

SETTING AND ACTION STYLE
Fight on one broad, empty rooftop plaza with wet paving and a low concrete parapet. The red torii and crimson moon remain consistent background landmarks.
Begin with action, no introduction. Fluid full-body anime movement, strong key poses, readable trajectories, believable weight and clear foot contact. The girl is nimble and mischievous; the robot is heavy and intimidating.
Use wide and medium shots to establish attack direction. Brief close-ups only for reactions and the sticker reveal. Maintain screen direction: girl generally left, robot right. Avoid random camera spins or excessive cuts.

TIMELINE

0–4 seconds:
Low wide shot. The robot's fist crashes into the pavement where the girl stood a moment earlier. She has already jumped sideways, clearing the impact before contact. Water and small stone fragments burst outward.
Track her short slide to a balanced landing. Her gaze flicks toward its upper-left chest. A quick sharp-toothed grin.

4–10 seconds:
Medium-wide lateral tracking shot. The robot makes two distinct claw swipes.
She ducks beneath the first, then deflects the second with her katana at an oblique angle, producing a brief shower of sparks. She redirects the claw rather than stopping the robot's full weight.
She reaches toward its chest with her free left hand. It immediately covers that area with its other hand and forces her back. Keep the sticker visible but do not isolate it in a reveal close-up yet.

10–17 seconds:
The robot lunges. She evades toward the nearby low parapet, plants one foot against its vertical face and pushes off.
Show the complete trajectory in a wide shot: wall push, short airborne arc, then one-foot contact on the robot's right shoulder.
The robot turns and reaches for her. She drops behind its shoulder before the claw arrives. Her coat follows with natural secondary motion.

17–23 seconds:
She lands on the paving beside the robot, bends her knees and immediately circles toward its front.
It raises one claw to intercept her sword. She deliberately presents the katana high in her right hand, drawing its guard upward.
Her eyes glance down toward the unprotected yellow sticker. Push into a medium two-shot that clearly shows the sword feint and her free left hand.

23–27 seconds:
Close-up of her LEFT fingertips catching the yellow sticker's edge on the robot's upper-left chest.
She peels it away in ONE continuous motion. The thin paper bends as the adhesive releases. Emphasize an unexpectedly small, crisp peeling sound.
The armor underneath is intact with a clean circular patch. The central chest mechanism remains lit. The robot is fully powered and unharmed.

27–30 seconds:
Medium two-shot, girl left foreground and robot right background.
She takes one step back and raises the stolen yellow smile sticker in her LEFT hand beside her face, printed side facing camera. Her katana remains lowered safely in her RIGHT hand.
She says, in the referenced girl's Japanese voice: 「もーらい。」
The robot freezes in stunned disbelief, then slowly tilts its head toward the empty patch on its chest. Its eye stays illuminated.
Hold the last composition long enough to read both reactions. She has NOT attached the sticker to anything yet.

AUDIO
Energetic instrumental electronic breakbeat with Japanese percussion, no vocals. Synchronize selected footfalls, metal impacts and sword deflections with the rhythm.
Abruptly drop the music at the sticker peel. Leave the tiny adhesive sound, her short line and an awkward mechanical whirr.
Only the girl's mouth moves for her dialogue. The robot expresses itself through head movement, eye light and electronic sounds.

END STATE — MUST MATCH PART 2
Girl standing screen-left, holding exactly one peeled yellow smile sticker in her left hand. Katana lowered in her right hand. Scabbard attached at her left hip. Pink star sticker still on her left sleeve.
Robot standing screen-right, intact and powered, with one clean empty patch on its upper-left chest.
Same rooftop, lighting, camera axis and background landmarks.

AVOID
No subtitles, captions, title cards, speech bubbles, UI, watermarks or added readable signage. Preserve established costume graphics without inventing new slogans.
No blood, injuries, dismemberment, armor destruction, transformation, extra limbs, character merging, teleportation or unexplained prop changes.
Do not turn the robot cute or make it cry before the sticker is removed.

--Part 2--
Create a 15-second continuation of the preceding 30-second anime video. Preserve its aspect ratio and visual style. This is the next moment in the same scene, not a new scene or a recap.

REFERENCE PRIORITY
The FOURTH attached image is the FINAL FRAME of the preceding 30-second video. Use it as the exact STARTING FRAME of this continuation.

Match its composition, camera angle, character positions, body orientation, facial expressions, hand positions, sword and scabbard state, sticker location, lighting, background and existing damage.

The girl's character sheet defines her identity, costume and proportions.
The robot's character sheet defines its identity, mechanical construction and proportions.
The attached girl's audio defines ONLY the girl's vocal timbre and pitch range. Do not repeat the recording's original words. The robot has no spoken dialogue.

The fourth image takes priority for the current scene state. Character sheets must not reset poses, restore removed stickers or undo changes already visible in the final frame.
Use the existing background reference for world design only; never replace the opening composition with a new establishing shot.

CONTINUITY
Begin by naturally animating the fourth image. No opening transition, pose reset, sudden camera jump or repeated sticker theft.
Maintain the exact established appearance of the stolen sticker: its color, shape, symbol and size. Do not redesign it.
There is only ONE stolen sticker. Track it continuously.
Use the hand already holding it in the starting frame. Never switch hands without showing the transfer.
If the sticker is already attached to the girl or her equipment, leave it there and show her admiring it instead of attaching another copy.
Continue the sword's existing state. If drawn, show one clear sheathing action before she uses both hands. If already sheathed, keep it sheathed.

STYLE AND COMEDY
High-quality hand-drawn Japanese 2D anime, fluid character acting, detailed painted anime background, consistent designs.
The battle is over. Reveal that the terrifying robot is upset about losing its favorite sticker.
Use a brief awkward pause and expressive body language. No explanatory narration or sentimental ending.

TIMELINE

0–4 seconds:
Continue directly from the supplied final frame with subtle natural movement.
The girl smugly admires the stolen sticker.
If she is still holding it, she presses it onto an accessible flat section of her scabbard, keeping its established size and showing the contact clearly. If already attached, she simply smooths it down.
Use the minimum movement necessary from the supplied pose. Do not replay the theft.
Behind her, the robot's shoulders begin trembling, initially suggesting an angry counterattack.

4–8 seconds:
The robot suddenly sits heavily on the ground and throws a childish tantrum.
Two short heel stomps. It points at the exact spot where the sticker was removed, then holds out an open hand toward the girl, demanding it back.
Its mechanical body and facial structure remain unchanged. Express distress through posture, head movement and plaintive electronic squeaks, not human speech or liquid tears.
The girl turns toward it. Her smug grin becomes a blank, slightly awkward expression.
Hold a short silent beat.

8–12 seconds:
The girl selects ONE small, visibly existing decorative sticker from her coat. Show its original position before removal. Use a design already present in the references; do not make a new sticker suddenly appear.
With her sword safely sheathed, she visibly peels this replacement sticker off her coat, steps closer and presses it onto the robot's original empty sticker spot.
Keep the stolen sticker attached to her equipment and unchanged.
She casually says in Japanese, using the supplied girl's voice:
「これでいい？」
Only her mouth moves for this line.

12–15 seconds:
The robot immediately stops protesting.
It looks down at the replacement sticker, then raises a clear thumbs-up using its existing articulated hand.
Its relaxed shoulders and pleased head tilt make its fixed jagged grin look delighted.
The girl gives her characteristic mischievous, sharp-toothed grin.
End with both characters and the exchanged stickers readable in the composition. Hold the final reaction briefly. No renewed combat.

CAMERA
Preserve the starting frame's camera axis and screen direction.
Move smoothly from the opening composition to a wider shot for the seated tantrum, then a medium shot for the replacement.
Prioritize clear hands, sticker contact and character reactions. No fast orbiting camera or excessive cuts.

AUDIO
Continue the preceding scene's ambience naturally.
Heavy seated thud, two heel impacts, small electronic whining, a crisp adhesive peel and a soft sticker pat.
A short pleased electronic chime accompanies the thumbs-up.
The girl says only 「これでいい？」.
No robot dialogue, narration or vocal music.

AVOID
No subtitles, captions, speech bubbles, title cards, interface graphics, watermarks or new readable text.
No duplicate stickers, spontaneous prop changes, invisible transfers, extra limbs, character redesign, transformation or teleportation.
Do not restore the stolen sticker to the robot.
Do not change the background, time of day or lighting.
No photorealism, live-action scenery or 3D toy rendering.

Seedance 2.5 Prompt
Create a 15-second, 16:9 cinematic action video set at Shibuya Scramble Crossing, Tokyo, at night.

CHARACTER REFERENCES
Use only the two character reference images for identity and design.
Reference 1: Character A, the yellow-and-black mechanical skull cyborg.
Reference 2: Character B, the towering skeletal king wearing crimson robes.

A: Approximately 180 cm tall. Chipped yellow industrial armor, horizontal pointed head extensions, skull mask, black breathing hoses, intricate mechanical joints, spiked shoulders, chains, and torn dark fabric.
B: Approximately 260 cm tall. Huge branching black antlers, ornate crown, glowing red eyes, exposed skeletal ribcage, elaborate tattered crimson robes, and an ornate staff.

Preserve their exact silhouettes, proportions, materials, colors, and accessories. Create fluid full-body combat animation and dynamic camera movement. Maintain their height difference.

VISUAL STYLE
Photorealistic live-action cinematography, spectacular destruction VFX, and explosive shonen battle intensity.

Extreme acceleration, brutal close-range punches, powerful blocks, violent recoil, and physical impacts that destroy roads and buildings.

Combine tactile physical realism with aggressive digital corruption: RGB separation, horizontal signal tearing, datamoshing trails, pixel fragmentation, scanline interference, and dirty electronic noise.
Keep the choreography and decisive impacts clearly readable.

GLITCH AND NOISE DIRECTION
Make the effects react to the action.

On punch contact: short, violent RGB displacement around the fighters, horizontal image shearing, and a burst of coarse digital static radiating from the impact.

During extreme acceleration: stretched datamoshing trails and fragmented afterimages attached to moving limbs. These are visual motion trails, not separate characters.

Around the reality fracture: unstable scanlines, displaced image strips, crawling pixel noise, and flickering red-white edges.
During mist transformation: mechanical surfaces break into tiny yellow particles, black vapor, and granular signal noise. The transition remains continuous and visibly follows the body.

During the final destruction: physical fragments mix with pixel breakup, corrupted motion trails, and a dense burst of electronic interference.

Use the strongest corruption in brief bursts, followed by clear moving imagery. Keep physical motion flowing through every effect. Avoid prolonged freezes or static poses.

LOCATION
An empty, rain-soaked Shibuya Scramble Crossing. Recognizable diagonal zebra crossings, giant LED billboards, QFRONT-style architecture, and surrounding shopping towers.

Wet asphalt reflects cold city lights, yellow sparks, and crimson energy.

Billboards briefly malfunction in response to nearby shockwaves: distorted footage, broken scanlines, and signal noise.

Keep the fight within this intersection. Environmental damage accumulates and remains visible.

0–3 SECONDS — EXPLOSIVE COLLISION
Begin immediately in motion.
An ultra-low camera races along the white crossing stripes as both fighters launch toward each other.

A’s fist crashes into B’s blocking forearm. Show clear contact and recoil, followed by an expanding pressure ring that blasts rainwater outward and fractures the asphalt.

At contact, deliver a sharp burst of RGB separation and horizontal signal tearing. Restore a clear image immediately as the movement continues.

Whip-pan into a side-on tracking shot. A drives a heavy punch into B’s guarded ribs.

B slides backward, tearing trenches through the road. The shockwave lifts asphalt slabs and bursts a nearby empty building’s glass facade.
Debris travels outward from the strike. Yellow motion trails and fragmented crimson afterimages emphasize their opposing momentum.

3–5 SECONDS — REALITY FRACTURE
B plants its foot, pivots, and swings its staff in a savage diagonal counterattack.

A crimson energy slash cuts across the viewer’s image plane, opening a glowing fracture through reality directly in front of A.

Shoot from an extreme low Dutch angle as the staff passes close to the lens.

Along the fracture, image strips slide out of alignment. Red-white pixels crawl across the edges. Horizontal static and displaced scanlines expose a narrow black slit.

A ducks beneath the slash.

The camera pushes toward A’s articulated metal hand as it catches the fractured edge and pulls the moving image open like a curtain.

This is a fracture in reality at the camera plane, not a broken billboard or ordinary glass.
5–8 SECONDS — BODY BECOMES MIST
Without pausing, A transforms its entire body into dense black industrial mist threaded with yellow sparks and tiny metal particles.

Feet and legs dissolve first, followed by torso and arms. Its skull and reaching hand disappear last.

Mechanical surfaces progressively fragment into smoky particles and granular digital noise. Show the physical anatomy continuously becoming vapor.

A’s former position becomes completely empty.

The mist flows through the opened fracture.

Rise into an overhead view of Shibuya’s diagonal crossings. Follow one coherent ribbon of black-and-yellow mist racing around B’s blind side and converging directly behind the king.

Use streaming pixel trails and localized datamoshing within the moving vapor. Keep its path and destination obvious.

8–10 SECONDS — REASSEMBLY AND COMBINATION
Dive into a low rear three-quarter angle behind B’s whipping crimson cape.
The mist converges and reconstructs A behind the king. Yellow particles condense into the original skull, armor, arms, and legs.

Digital noise contracts into the mechanical surfaces and disappears as each part becomes solid.

A immediately attacks. B pivots toward the movement.

From over A’s yellow shoulder, show a left body punch connecting with B’s ribs, followed by a compact elbow that snaps the king’s upper body sideways.

Each contact creates a brief pulse of image displacement, metallic sparks, and dirty static. Keep the connecting fist, cracking bone, and recoil visible.

Arc toward a clear three-quarter side angle as A plants its foot and draws back its right fist.

10–13 SECONDS — FINAL PUNCH AND COMPLETE DESTRUCTION
A steps forward and drives one decisive rising right straight into B’s sternum.

Show unmistakable fist-to-bone contact from a powerful low angle.
Use a fraction of a second of slow motion at contact, then accelerate into explosive destruction.

A concentrated glitch pulse erupts from the contact point: RGB channels split outward, the surrounding image briefly shears horizontally, and coarse electronic noise follows the expanding shockwave.

B’s ribcage caves inward and shatters outward.

Cracks race through its spine, skull, crown, antlers, arms, and legs. The entire skeletal king physically breaks into thousands of small fragments and fine powder.

Its staff splinters. Its crimson robes tear into scattered scraps.

Mix the flying physical fragments with brief pixel breakup and corrupted motion trails. Show the destruction clearly; the king must visibly shatter rather than simply disappear.

The same impact creates a massive radial shockwave across Shibuya. Asphalt buckles into a crater. Crossing slabs erupt. Nearby empty building facades collapse, and billboard supports bend and fall.

A remains solid and intact through the follow-through.
13–15 SECONDS — AFTERMATH
Pull back into a ground-level wide shot of the devastated intersection.

A stands alone in the crater, slowly lowering its fist as rain and dust move through the damaged city lights.

Only tiny bone chips, snapped antler fragments, broken crown pieces, and torn crimson cloth remain of B.

The king is completely pulverized. No intact skull, body, crown, or antlers remain. It does not regenerate.

Let the aggressive digital interference decay into faint grain and residual noise on damaged billboards.

Finish with a slow camera drift around A’s yellow-and-black silhouette while debris settles around its feet.

CAMERA
Use ground-level tracking, extreme low angles, a hand close-up, an overhead reveal, an over-the-shoulder attack, and a clear final impact angle.

Connect cuts through movement and preserve spatial continuity.

Use selective motion blur during acceleration, crisp silhouettes at contact, and camera shake precisely on impact.

SOUND
Heavy metallic punches, sharp bone fractures, tearing digital distortion, rushing mist, deep shockwaves, collapsing concrete, and raining glass.

Synchronize short bitcrushed crackles and electronic noise with the glitch bursts.
Build aggressive industrial percussion through the fight. Drop the music at the final punch, exposing the impact and destruction. Finish with rain, settling debris, and fading electrical interference.

FINAL REQUIREMENTS
Full-screen 16:9 moving cinematic video.
No dialogue, subtitles, added titles, or watermarks.
Preserve character identity through every glitch.
Maintain continuous physical motion and readable combat.
Show full-body mist transformation, directional travel, and complete reconstruction.
Major environmental destruction follows visible impacts.
The yellow cyborg survives.
The skeletal king is completely pulverized.

Seedance 2.5 Prompt
Create a 15-second, 16:9 psychedelic horror music video: 30 distinct animated compositions, an average of 0.5 seconds per shot. Start at full intensity on the first frame. Make the supplied artworks come violently alive inside a corrupted, hypnotic nightmare.

REFERENCE DIRECTION
Use all supplied images as visual references. Preserve their recognizable silhouettes, intricate ornament, chrome surfaces, skulls, horns, jeweled details, printed textures, deep blacks, blood-red accents and electric rainbow colors. Develop additional compositions from these motifs to reach 30 shots. Preserve the mix of photographic detail and graphic illustration. Each shot fills the screen.
MOTION PRIORITY
The subjects themselves must move, not just the camera. Use one dominant, instantly readable action per shot:

Horned figures snap their heads toward the viewer; metallic blindfolds ripple and ribbons whip outward.
Chrome mouths open abruptly; keys twist, chains swing and skull-shaped jewelry vibrates.

Uncanny deer jerk forward; antlers branch rapidly and nearby plants coil inward.
Skeletal warriors slash across the frame; armor plates shift and radial patterns spin behind them.
A psychedelic mechanical tunnel contracts and pulls the camera through its center.
Giant cybernetic skulls loom over a neon city; jaw mechanisms snap and buildings bend around them.
Chrome bird-skull creatures thrust their beaks toward the lens; segmented necks coil and unfold.
A skeletal astronaut snaps toward camera as neon vapor pours through the helmet.
Striped cakes twist like living sculptures; cream stretches, cherries levitate and red syrup flows upward.
Horned skull idols rotate abruptly; ornaments orbit their faces and printed layers slip out of registration.
An ornate oiran-like figure turns sharply; hair ornaments vibrate, sleeves whip and metallic ribs expand.
A jeweled black cat fixes its gaze on the viewer, then lunges toward the lens as its ornaments scatter into light.
Use different actions and framing when a motif returns. Make every scene visibly animate from its first frame. Keep the main subject recognizable beneath the distortion.
EDITING / 15-SECOND STRUCTURE
0.0-3.0s: 5 shots, approximately 0.6s each. Open with an extreme close-up of a horned face snapping toward camera on the first kick. Cut through a metallic mouth, a deer, a skeletal warrior and a tunnel. Immediate impact; no intro.
3.0-6.0s: 6 shots, alternating approximately 0.4s and 0.6s. Neon city skulls, chrome bird creatures, astronaut and cat. Hard cuts, whip-pan transitions and sudden changes of scale.
6.0-9.0s: 6 shots, alternating approximately 0.4s and 0.6s. Warping desserts, horned idols and the ornate figure. Surfaces stretch, liquefy and snap back. Push through an eye, mouth or spiral into the next composition.
9.0-12.0s: 6 shots, alternating approximately 0.4s and 0.6s. Return to earlier motifs with more aggressive actions, extreme close-ups, inverted viewpoints and brief kaleidoscopic multiplication.
12.0-15.0s: 7 shots: six approximately 0.4s shots followed by a 0.6s final shot. Maximum kinetic intensity. End with a horned skull rushing into the lens, the image tearing into chromatic fragments, then an abrupt cut to black on the final distorted impact. No fade.

GLITCH / NOISE
Dense, deliberate analog and digital corruption: RGB channel separation, horizontal scanline tears, VHS tracking errors, CRT interference, granular static, datamosh trails, pixel-sorting streaks, block displacement, color inversion, frame skipping and short motion echoes. Place strong glitches on cuts, kicks and snare fills. Use brief 1-3-frame disruptions and textured noise bursts while keeping the subjects visible. Distortion must react to moving forms. Alternate crisp, disturbing detail with explosive corruption. Avoid prolonged full-screen white flashes.

CAMERA
Aggressive crash zooms, rapid lateral whip pans, short barrel rolls, macro-to-wide jumps and forward dives through openings. Choose one main camera move per shot. Preserve clear focal points and deep layered motion.
AUDIO
Original instrumental EDM / dark psychedelic trance at 150 BPM. Start immediately with a heavy four-on-the-floor kick and tight rolling sixteenth-note bass. Add distorted acid arpeggios, unsettling resonant synths, metallic percussion, reverse swells and granular digital noise. Synchronize cuts, subject impacts and glitches to beats and offbeats. Increase density toward the final second. No vocals, speech or narration.
AVOID
Static slideshow frames, simple Ken Burns motion, slow motion, gentle crossfades, long establishing shots, cute cheerful mood, generic smooth plastic rendering, persistent split screens, contact-sheet layouts, added captions, titles, subtitles, logos and watermarks.

Seedance 2.5 Prompt
Create a 15-second, 16:9 cinematic battle between the two characters in the attached reference images, set in a destructible Manhattan street. Photorealistic materials, explosive superhuman martial arts, aerial combat, smoke teleportation, and visceral action-film cinematography.

REFERENCE IMAGES AND CHARACTER CONSISTENCY
Use the reference sheets strictly for character appearance. Render exactly one fighter from each reference as a fully realized character inside the scene. Do not display the design sheets, their panels, labels, or typography.
Character A — Mechanical Fox-Mask Ninja, reference image 1:
Preserve the white-and-red fox mask, glowing red eyes, black mechanical armor, white armor accents, intricate brass details, thick cable-like hair, respirator components, ragged red-and-black fabric, and katana. Fast, precise, aggressive movement.

Character B — Decayed Antlered Warrior, reference image 2:
Preserve the ivory skeletal body, skull face, enormous branching antlers, intertwined dead branches, weathered off-white robes, ornaments, and sheathed swords. Visibly taller than the ninja. Heavy, devastating physical power. Maintain the same anatomy, costume, and silhouette throughout the battle.
LOCATION AND VISUAL LANGUAGE
A Manhattan intersection at blue hour: towering glass facades, yellow taxis, streetlights, steam rising from subway grates, and long views between skyscrapers. Keep the action within this recognizable intersection and the airspace immediately above it.

Destruction must follow the attacks: punches launch bodies into architecture, impacts fracture asphalt, and shockwaves shatter nearby windows. Heavy debris falls with convincing weight.
SMOKE TELEPORTATION RULE
Only the fox-mask ninja uses smoke teleportation. His entire body dissolves into dense black smoke threaded with red embers, then reforms as a solid, intact body at another position.

Smoke clouds linger where he disappears. He can return to these previously established locations. Establish three recognizable smoke positions during the early exchanges, then reuse them during the final counterattack. These are successive appearances of ONE ninja, never clones.
TIMELINE — EXACTLY 15 SECONDS

0.0–2.0 seconds — IMMEDIATE IMPACT
Begin on the antlered warrior’s fist already striking the ninja’s armored torso. The impact launches the ninja backward over a yellow taxi and into a building facade. Glass and masonry burst outward.

Start with a low, wide-angle street-level shot, then accelerate alongside the airborne ninja. Show the impact clearly before the debris expands. No introduction or preparatory posing.
2.0–5.0 seconds — SMOKE TELEPORT COMBAT
The warrior charges toward the damaged facade. Just before his follow-up punch connects, the ninja dissolves into black smoke.

The ninja reforms behind the warrior and lands a powerful rising knee, lifting him off the street. He immediately dissolves again and reappears overhead, driving a heel downward. Establish lingering ember-filled smoke clouds at the departure positions.

Use an over-the-shoulder view, a motivated whip-pan to the rear attack, then a wider upward view between the skyscrapers. Both fighters remain identifiable through each transition.

5.0–8.0 seconds — BRUTAL REVERSAL
The warrior catches the descending ninja by the ankle and violently swings him down into the intersection. Asphalt fractures outward and a nearby taxi slides sideways from the shockwave.
Follow the downward motion from above, then cut to a low angle for the ground impact. The ninja disappears inside black smoke and rising dust. The warrior stands over the crater, apparently victorious. Let the impact sound decay into a brief hush.

8.0–12.0 seconds — THE SMOKE TRAP
Red embers ignite inside the smoke clouds left earlier.

In one readable medium-wide view, the ninja reappears from the rear cloud and kicks the warrior forward, vanishes, reforms from the side cloud and punches his ribs, then vanishes and reforms directly in front of him.
Three rapid, distinct positions. Every attack connects before the next teleport. The warrior staggers, unable to recover between hits. The ninja finishes firmly planted in front of him, hand gripping the katana hilt.

Accelerate the rhythm through these attacks. Use short whip-pans and decisive impact cuts while maintaining clear geography.

12.0–15.0 seconds — DECISIVE FINISH
Briefly slow the instant before the ninja draws his sword. Return to full speed for one clean, devastating slash across the warrior’s torso, leaving a thin red trail.

A short still beat. A crack races through the warrior’s skull and antlers. His skeletal body and branches fracture into dry ivory fragments and collapse completely. The warrior is definitively defeated.
The ninja remains standing and begins to sheath his sword as damaged masonry falls behind him. End on a sharp close-up of the fox mask’s glowing red eye.

GLITCH AND NOISE
Synchronize effects with physical events:
During disappearance, the ninja’s silhouette briefly tears sideways before dissolving into smoke.
During reappearance, a red chromatic afterimage resolves into the solid body.
At major impacts, add a very brief frame tear, digital noise burst, and sharp audio distortion.

Keep faces, striking limbs, contact points, and the final collapse readable. Preserve the cinematic image between these short disruptions.
CAMERA AND SOUND
Combine ground-level wide angles, shoulder-level tracking, an overhead descent, controlled whip-pans, and selective speed ramps. Each camera movement follows an attack or reveals a teleport destination.

Sound: heavy metallic impacts, rushing air, pressure-wave bass, breaking glass, asphalt cracking, mechanical movement, a sharp sword draw, and brittle bone fracture. A tiny silence immediately before the final slash, followed by a powerful impact and debris falling.

No dialogue, captions, subtitles, logos, watermarks, split screens, character duplication, extra limbs, costume changes, blood, or flesh. No regeneration after the final defeat.

A reaches B in midair and attacks with both katana in a rapid crossing motion.
B dissolves into black mist before the blades contact the armor.
A passes through the vanishing silhouette.
A missed blade shears a billboard support, exposing a clean silver metal edge.
The enormous sign tilts away from its mounting.
CAMERA:
Cut to a wide lateral tracking shot.
Keep both fighters, the billboard structure, and the drop to the street visible.

[00:03–00:04]
ACTION:
B reappears above and behind A and swings the scythe downward.
A twists in midair and catches it with crossed katana.
Show a small cool-white reflection at the blade contact, without any flying particles.
The impact throws A through an LED billboard framework.
Steel bends and dark screen panels break into rigid rectangular pieces.
CAMERA:
Continue with a sharp upward pan to B, then follow A sideways.
Show the weapon contact clearly before tracking the collision with the structure.

[00:04–00:05]
ACTION:
A catches one boot against the exposed maintenance platform and kicks off.
The platform tears from its anchors.
A intercepts B in open air with a fast two-strike combination.
B blocks the first katana with the scythe shaft.
A rotates around the block and immediately attacks from the opposite side.
CAMERA:
Cut to a side medium-wide tracking shot showing both complete figures.
Follow their crossing trajectories and distinguish the two weapon contacts.

[00:05–00:06]
ACTION:
B dissolves before the second strike lands and reforms directly behind A.
B drives the scythe shaft across A's raised guard.
A is launched through an upper-floor glass facade.
Window frames bend, glass fractures, and concrete breaks from the opening.
A's armor shows dry metallic scratches and shallow dents.
CAMERA:
Continue with a fast pan to B's new position.
Track A's lateral flight into the facade impact.
Keep A visible through the thin gray dust.

[00:06–00:07]
ACTION:
A hits an interior wall feet-first and rebounds without pausing.
The wall caves inward as A launches back through the broken exterior.
A returns to open air with both swords extended.
A large facade section collapses below while B approaches from the opposite direction.
CAMERA:
Continue tracking along the building exterior.
Catch A bursting back out, then widen slightly as the fighters converge.

[00:07–00:08]
ACTION:
A and B clash in midair through three rapid contacts:
A's right katana strikes the scythe shaft.
A's left katana catches the returning blade.
A drives an armored knee into B's chest housing.

The knee dents the metal casing and loosens several clearly shaped silver fasteners.
The fasteners tumble individually rather than forming a particle spray.
B recoils and begins dissolving into black mist.
CAMERA:
Cut to a lateral aerial tracking shot.
Match the fighters' travel against the rushing buildings.
Use brief camera vibration and physical recoil to emphasize each contact.

[00:08–00:09]
ACTION:
B reforms below A and swings the scythe upward.
A tucks both legs and twists through a tight aerial roll.
The scythe passes beneath A and cuts through sign rigging.
A heavy metal structure falls away while A extends toward a projecting building ledge.
CAMERA:
Continue with a controlled downward tilt to reveal B below.
Follow A's roll while retaining the rising scythe and falling structure.

[00:09–00:10]
ACTION:
B teleports above A and dives with a two-handed scythe strike.
A kicks off the ledge and escapes sideways.
B's attack continues downward into the intersection.
A broad crater opens, asphalt plates lift, and cracks spread across the crossroads.
Concrete and road fragments follow heavy, clearly visible arcs.
CAMERA:
Follow the descending scythe with a fast downward tilt.
Show A escaping near the upper edge before revealing the street impact.

[00:10–00:11]
ACTION:
A briefly plants a boot against a slanted billboard support and launches into another aerial arc.
B dissolves inside the crater below.
Black mist rises and gathers behind A's flight path.
A turns the eyes toward it before rotating the body.
CAMERA:
Cut to a low front three-quarter aerial view.
Include the ruined intersection below and the gathering mist behind A's shoulder.

[00:11–00:12]
ACTION:
Still airborne, A rotates the hips and shoulders into a diagonal katana strike.
The blade begins moving toward apparently empty space.
B's ceramic mask, manufactured antlers, armor, and scythe begin reassembling directly along the approaching blade's path.
A has anticipated the teleport.
CAMERA:
Continue with a short arc around A.
Settle into a clear side three-quarter view connecting the sword trajectory to B's reassembly point.

[00:12–00:13]
ACTION:
B becomes solid at the exact instant A's katana arrives.
The blade cuts diagonally through the ceramic mask and central metal chassis.
Show a clean mechanical fracture line, exposed silver edges, and several distinct white ceramic chips.
No sparks or colored emissions occur.

The opening reveals gears, brackets, and circuit boards.
The damaged assembly begins separating along the cut.
Use only a roughly 0.15-second slowdown within this beat to clarify the contact.
CAMERA:
Briefly stabilize the aerial composition.
Show the blade entering the artificial armor, passing through the chassis, and exiting.
Keep the contact and mechanical fracture unobscured.

[00:13–00:14]
ACTION:
Return immediately to full speed.
A continues the rotation into a devastating spinning kick against B's compromised central chassis.

The entire machine breaks apart.

The ceramic mask fractures into angular white chips.
The manufactured antlers snap into short, rigid metal sections.
Armor housings split into silver and dark steel pieces.
Gears, small motors, brackets, and circuit-board fragments separate from the collapsing internal frame.

Show recognizable solid components breaking free and rotating independently.
The fragments scatter outward, then descend under gravity.
A thin cloud of pale gray ceramic dust follows more slowly.

No luminous particle burst, colored spray, fluid movement, or fireball.
The scythe is released as B loses all structural integrity.
Hard debris strikes the weakened building behind B, triggering another facade collapse.
CAMERA:
Cut to a medium-wide aerial view, keeping B large enough to recognize the mechanical breakup.
Show the kick making contact before pulling back.
Clearly reveal the ceramic mask, antler assemblies, armor, and internal mechanisms fracturing.

[00:14–00:15]
ACTION:
A descends through falling mechanical fragments and lands in the ruined intersection.
The landing buckles the asphalt beneath both boots.
B's abandoned scythe falls behind A and embeds in the road, splitting a slab.
The suspended vessel and chains swing.

A lowers both katana.
Only scattered mechanical components, white ceramic chips, and dry gray dust remain of B.
The last black mist disperses completely.
Damaged building sections continue falling in the background.
CAMERA:
Continue downward with A's landing.
Settle into a stable low-angle composition with A in the foreground, the scythe behind, and the destroyed intersection beyond.
End on the completed mechanical destruction.

CLIMAX MATERIAL AND MOTION RULES
The finishing sequence must remain clear:
katana cuts artificial armor and chassis → spinning kick collapses the weakened structure → the complete machine shatters into small rigid components.

B's face is a ceramic mask.
The antlers are manufactured metal assemblies.
The chest is an armored machine housing.
All visible interior details are mechanical.

Destruction fragments must have:
hard edges, rigid shapes, neutral colors, visible thickness, independent rotation, and downward gravitational motion.

Prioritize silver metal, dark steel, white ceramic, black cable pieces, and recognizable electronic components.
Use sparse, thin pale-gray dust.
Avoid dense sprays of tiny particles.

Keep red and yellow reference details on intact rigid surfaces only.
Do not create colored trails from damaged armor or electronic lights.
Do not tint airborne debris with red billboard reflections.

No intact enemy figure remains.
B does not regenerate, escape, or reassemble.
The black mist does not replace the physical breakup.
The abandoned scythe may remain separately.

ENVIRONMENTAL DESTRUCTION
Use collapsing building corners, broken columns, falling floor edges, rigid LED screen panels, twisted billboard frames, shattered storefronts, deep road trenches, and craters.
Every destruction event follows visible contact, a collision, a rebound, or falling debris.
Keep concrete, glass, metal, ceramic, and black mist visually distinct.
Preserve enough visibility to follow the fighters.

AUDIO
Use sharp katana movements, heavy scythe movement, dry metallic clashes, mechanical servos, armored impacts, and powerful wall rebounds.
Add glass breaking, concrete fractures, bending steel, falling billboard structures, road rupture, and heavy rubble impacts.
Teleportation produces a short inward rush followed by a compact pressure pulse.

The final cut sounds like ceramic cracking and metal shearing.
The finishing kick produces a dry, powerful crash of armor, gears, ceramic plates, and electronic components.
Mechanical fragments land with distinct clinks and hard impacts.
End with rubble settling and the ringing chains of the scythe.

Background music is optional.
Keep environmental sound and action effects clear and dominant.
No dialogue or narration.

EXCLUSIONS
No flying sparks, glowing particle trails, warm-colored impact particles, or full-frame flashes.
No liquid spray, droplets, splashes, dripping, or wet impact effects.
No blood, biological tissue, real bones, or anatomical damage.
No weightless hovering, prolonged posing, continuous slow motion, or random camera spinning.
No duplicated characters, extra limbs, changing weapons, or identity swaps.
No teleportation or mist transformation for A.
No reference-sheet borders, annotations, subtitles, title cards, or watermarks.
Preserve the reference designs and the recognizable daytime Times Square setting.
