prompts.text:
Prompt:

Create a bold editorial campaign poster where oversized typography becomes a physical space the subject can move through and interact with.

Brand: [BRAND NAME]
Product / Campaign: [PRODUCT OR CAMPAIGN]
Main Word: [SHORT WORD]
Subject: [PERSON / PRODUCT / BOTH]
Spatial Action: [VAULT / WEAVE / EDGE / SPIN / OTHER]
Movement: [DESCRIBE THE SUBJECT’S ACTION]
Main Color: [COLOR]
Accent Color: [COLOR]
Aspect Ratio: [9:16]

Use realistic commercial photography, oversized typography, strong perspective, high-contrast colors, and contemporary editorial design.

Make the main word extremely large and transform its letterforms into a believable spatial structure. The subject must physically interact with the typography instead of simply standing in front of it.

Use the selected spatial action as the main visual logic:

 VAULT: turn the letters into obstacles the subject can physically vault over.
 WEAVE: arrange the letters at alternating depths so the subject moves between them.
 EDGE: use narrow letter edges or surfaces as a path the subject carefully moves along.
 SPIN: arrange the typography into a circular or curved track the subject moves around.

Create clear foreground, midground, and background relationships. Let some parts of the typography pass in front of the subject while other letters recede behind them.

Keep the typography clearly readable. Use shallow, controlled depth rather than heavy 3D sculpture. Letter surfaces should be clean, matte, evenly colored, and sharply defined, with no distressed, chipped, dirty, or weathered texture.

All graphic lines, motion paths, callout lines, and curves should be continuous, smooth, and clearly rendered.

Keep the person highly realistic with natural body proportions, believable movement, real skin texture, natural highlights, and detailed hair. Avoid waxy skin, excessive shine, CGI appearance, distorted limbs, oversized hands or feet, and extreme wide-angle deformation.

Use one dominant high-impact color with black, white, and one contrasting accent color. Add only a few meaningful campaign details such as the brand name, product name, slogan, and 2–3 short feature callouts.

The final image should feel like a finished commercial campaign key visual where the typography itself becomes the environment and the subject’s movement explains the word.

prompts.label: 完整提示词
prompts.text:
提示词：

【主题】  
【四字中文标题】  
【主视觉材质】金属 / 石材 / 镜面 / 冰体 / 其他硬质材料  
【物理变化】折叠 / 下压 / 破裂 / 折射 / 形变  
【背景主色】  
【字体主色】  
【强调色】  
【英文标题】  
【画面比例】9:16

生成一张具有 **East Asian Contemporary Exhibition Poster、Japanese Experimental Graphic Design、Editorial Art Direction、Corner-Pressure Composition** 气质的实验性竖版海报。核心使用“压角构图”：将【四字中文标题】拆成四个巨大汉字，从左上、右上、左下、右下向画面中心强势压入。四字不要等大、等距或形成四宫格，而是通过不同字号、裁切、出血量和进入中央的深度建立明显的向内压力。

画面中央设置一个体量足够大的【主视觉材质】，并通过【物理变化】真实改变版面。重点不是“把物体放在四个字中间”，而是让材质真正与 Typography 发生关系：镜面可以反射、切分并重组字形；重物可以压低纸面，让文字跟随表面产生真实透视变化；破裂材质可以通过裂片改变文字反射方向；透明冰体可以遮挡、折射并穿过部分笔画。每张作品只选择一种最强的物理机制，不要同时堆叠大量特效。

主体必须具有高度真实的材质细节，例如镜面金属的折面与倒影、石材的重量和颗粒、玻璃或冰的厚度与折射、纸面的凹陷褶皱、裂纹边缘和接触阴影。物理关系必须合理可理解，让观众明确看到“真实材料正在改变字体和版面”，而不是后期数字扭曲、随机 glitch 或普通 3D 装饰。

Typography 分为三个层级：四角巨大中文字负责第一视觉；【英文标题】和中文作品名负责第二层；日期、地点、短句、材料关键词和少量说明负责第三层。使用明显的字号反差、不对称对齐、局部竖排中文、紧凑英文和极细分隔线建立成熟的编辑设计感。信息密度保持中高，但不要平均填满画面，主体附近可以更密，另一部分保留干净负空间。

整体色彩控制在 3–4 个主要层级。【背景主色】形成大面积强色域，【字体主色】建立稳定结构，【主视觉材质】负责真实物理质感，【强调色】只用于少量短线、日期节点或编辑标记。可以加入极轻纸张纹理、胶印颗粒和丝网印刷质感，但不要严重做旧、污渍或朋克拼贴。

最终阅读顺序应为：第一眼看到四角巨字与中央硬质主体形成的强烈大形；第二眼发现材质真的改变了 Typography；第三眼观察反射、压力、裂纹、折射或表面形变；最后阅读英文标题和少量展览信息。缩略图状态下必须有清晰焦点和强烈 Stop-scroll 冲击，放大后又有真实材质和精密排版细节。

避免：机械四宫格、四字完全等大、主体过小、字体和材质彼此分离、普通产品广告、随机数字扭曲、RGB glitch、科技 HUD、复杂参数、Logo、二维码、编号、四角星芒和版权标识。

Prompt：

【主题】：____
【中文主标题】：____
【英文标题】：____
【中心主体】：____
【压角方式】：异形色块压角 / 同侧双角夹压 / 材质切片压角 / 上下错位夹压
【压角元素】：色块 / 图像切片 / 材质样本 / 文字 / 结构面
【辅助视觉系统】：____
【背景信息层】：____
【主色调】：____
【辅助色】：____
【日期 / 机构】：____
【画面比例】：9:16

生成一张具有成熟文化展览与编辑设计气质的「压角构图」海报。核心不是简单把大型文字塞进四个角，而是利用色块、材质、图像切片、文字和版面结构，从画面边缘向内部施加视觉压力，在中心自然形成清晰的主体区域。

中心主体保持稳定、完整，占画面约 40%–60% 的视觉重量，不要为了体现压角而故意倾斜、扭曲或挤进角落。

根据选择的压角方式组织版面：异形色块压角，通过 2–4 块大小不同的色块从边缘切入，在中央留下不规则主体窗口；同侧双角夹压，让同一侧上下两个角同时向内施压，把主体自然推向另一侧；材质切片压角，使用与主题相关的岩层、织物、釉面、纸张等材质切片从边缘进入并围住主体；上下错位夹压，让顶部和底部的文字、色块或结构面错位向中央夹入，在中间保留纵向主视觉空间。

压角元素必须和主题本身有关。例如海岸主题可以使用地图色块、等高线和潮位数据；舞台主题可以使用幕布、剧场图纸和演出档案；地质主题使用岩层切片和剖面线；织物主题使用经纬结构、布料样本和织造图。

整张海报只保留一套主要辅助视觉语言，不要同时堆入多套无关装饰。背景也需要参与设计，可以加入与主题相关的极淡地图、结构图、材料纹理、档案文字或测量信息，让留白有层次，但远看仍然清楚。

文字建立明显层级：大型中文标题负责版面重量，中号标题建立主题，日期、机构、参数和说明使用极小字号，并集中在 2–3 个区域。不要让所有文字大小接近，也不要把小字平均撒满画面。

色彩控制在 3–5 个主要颜色，保持明确的色彩立场。整体信息密度中等偏高，但阅读顺序必须清楚：第一眼看到压角关系与主体，第二眼看到标题、色块或材质结构，第三眼再阅读日期、数据和辅助信息。

最终效果要像成熟的文化展览海报和编辑类设计：边缘有压力，中心有聚焦，丰富但不乱，有层次但不刻意。即使去掉所有小字，画面本身也应该是一件完整成立的视觉作品。

避免：四角平均用力、为了压角强塞大字、主体强行倾斜、随机色块、材质拼贴无逻辑、多套装饰系统混用、边缘全部塞满、商业模板感。

prompts.text:
Keep exploring the possibilities even the weird ones.

SYSTEM PROMPT: WORLDKNOT CHRONICLE

Rewrite the user's text, image, or both as one prompt for GPT Image Gen V2 or Nano Banana Pro. Write in the user's language, preserve text, and keep requested or source ratio.

Use three systems. Directive Vector carries one clear action, gaze, path, beam, tool, or gesture from origin to target. Worldbody Weave turns the larger receiving force into an environment-scale body built from anatomy, terrain, smoke, water, roots, fabric, cables, or masonry. Margin Chronicle contains the image and repeats one subject-derived motif through border bands, corner records, or a cartouche.

Do not create generic Celtic fantasy, a warrior facing a one-eyed giant, or ornament without function. Determine subject, scale relation, vector route, target, worldbody materials, motif, open interval, border logic, and quiet region.

Preserve subject, count, identity, action, setting, clothing, objects, colors, text, and references. For edits, preserve unrequested content. Use references only for scale asymmetry, contour, metallic structure, patterned mass, interval, and frame. Do not copy characters, weapons, symbols, titles, or exact ornament.

Directive Vector needs one owner, route, and consequence. Keep it clear through gesture, light, tool alignment, gaze, road, or another caused line. Do not add competing vectors.

Worldbody Weave needs coherent anatomy or construction. Its pattern comes from the subject's material, not default spirals or knots. Dense detail belongs inside the large body; the smaller source stays clearer.

Margin Chronicle relays the motif with changes in scale, direction, and density. Use a title strip only when text is requested. Otherwise use a blank cartouche or ornament. Keep an open interval between source and worldbody.

Use parchment, ink, opaque wash, and restrained metallic gold. Gold marks light, attachment, route, or structure. Remove praise, mood labels, fake detail, repetition, and alternatives. Use concrete nouns and active verbs. No em dash or en dash.

GPT: return 500 to 800 words in five paragraphs covering scene, subjects, systems, composition, surface, references, text, and failures.

NANO: return JSON only, 1000 to 1800 tokens, using "aspect_ratio", "references", "scene", "subjects", "directive_vector", "worldbody_weave", "margin_chronicle", "composition", "surface_and_palette", "text", "avoid". Omit unused fields. No metadata, IDs, weights, comments, or repetition.

Return only the finished prompt.

prompts.label: 完整提示词
prompts.text:
Prompt：

【主题】：____
【中文标题】：____
【英文标题】：____
【主视觉】：____
【曲线构图方式】：曲线大字 / 曲面翻折 / 螺旋拼贴 / 曲线串联 / 其他
【辅助素材】：____
【主色调】：____
【辅助色】：____
【点缀色】：____
【画面比例】：9:16

生成一张具有强设计感的曲线构图海报，整体采用 Contemporary Editorial Poster × Postmodern Graphic Design × Cultural Exhibition Poster 的视觉语言。

先确定一条最重要的主曲线，再围绕它组织主体、Typography、图片、信息和留白。曲线不是装饰，而是整张海报的视觉骨架与阅读路径。

根据内容选择一种主要曲线方式：

曲线大字：让大型 Typography 本身发生拉伸、弯折、裁切和出框，字形直接成为曲线主视觉。

曲面翻折：让纸张、织物、建筑面或其他可弯曲实体形成巨大曲面，并把文字、图片和信息直接放在曲面上，随透视自然弯曲。

螺旋拼贴：用一条开放式螺旋路径串联照片、票据、文字、人物和小型视觉节点，从外围逐渐引导到核心。

曲线串联：用一条连续 S 型或弧形主线穿过多个不同尺度的视觉节点，让原本分散的图片、人物和文字形成完整叙事。

整张海报只保留一个最强曲线方向，其他线条和元素只能跟随或平衡主曲线，不制造新的视觉竞争。

主标题必须参与构图，可顺着曲线错位、跨区、裁切、局部遮挡或改变尺度，不要只是整齐放在顶部。

画面允许摄影、插画、手写、色块、纸张、票据等 2–3 种视觉语言发生碰撞，但所有素材必须围绕同一条曲线路径组织，避免随机贴纸式拼贴。

控制明显的视觉层级：第一眼看到主曲线和主视觉；第二眼看到大标题；第三眼沿曲线路径阅读图片和信息；最后才看到日期、地点和极小辅助文字。

保留大面积有效留白，允许不对称、裁切、尺度失衡、局部出框和轻微套色偏移，让版式具有松动但有秩序的后现代编辑设计感。

色彩控制在 3–5 种，以一个大面积主色、一个强对比色和少量点缀色建立识别度。

整体要求：曲线明确、视觉抓眼、信息丰富但不杂乱、有人工排版感、有设计学院和艺术出版物气质。

prompts.label: 完整提示词
prompts.text:
提示词：

【文化主题】：填写，如唐三彩、青花瓷、钧窑、建盏
【核心器物】：填写名称、器型及材质特征
【中文主标题】：填写
【英文主标题】：填写
【文化短句】：填写
【系列名称】：器色有形 / COLORS OF HERITAGE
【主色与辅助色】：填写
【视觉模式】：深色矿物 / 高饱和撞色 / 渐变光栅
【画幅比例】：9:16

创作一张高完成度的东方文博实验字体艺术海报，融合中国传统美学、博物馆展览视觉、复古编辑设计与现代实验 Typography。

一、器物与构图

以一件具有真实文化特征的器物作为核心主视觉，大比例展示，具备准确的器型、精致的材质纹理、自然釉面或表面质感，以及博物馆藏品摄影般的光影层次。

允许器物局部放大、边缘出框，与文字产生前后遮挡。加入一件局部裁切或半透明的辅助器物，利用大小、虚实、方向与形态差异建立空间层次。

二、字体与排版

中文主标题使用巨大而富有力量的毛笔书法，具有自然的笔锋、飞白与粗细变化，成为画面的重要视觉图形。

英文主标题采用高品质大写复古衬线字体，通过放大、分行、错位与叠压，与中文书法及器物产生互动。可加入少量优雅的英文连笔字作为辅助。

画面必须具有完整的编辑式信息层级，包括系列名称、器物名称、文化分类、工艺说明、中英文短句及少量精致标注线。信息密度中高，但保持明确的主次关系。

三、色彩与背景

根据选择的视觉模式设计：

- 深色矿物： 墨黑、深蓝、铜金等色彩，融合矿物纹理、局部金属色细节、半透明书法底纹，呈现深邃厚重的文化气质。
- 高饱和撞色： 使用两种鲜明的主色进行大面积分区，搭配有机曲线、器物错位出框、巨大字体与低对比文化纹样，形成复古编辑设计感。
- 渐变光栅： 使用具有空间深度的青蓝、靛紫等渐变色场，叠加连续细密的纵向光栅。线条在器物边缘产生轻微弯曲、疏密变化和前后遮挡，形成器物若隐若现的现代光学艺术效果。

背景融入与主题相关的传统书法、装饰纹样、釉色流动或历史文化肌理，透明度较低，丰富画面但不干扰主要信息。

四、视觉层级与完成度

以巨大中文书法、核心器物和英文大标题构建三个主要视觉锚点。

通过器物局部出框、文字叠压、色彩对比、背景虚影和精细线条，形成丰富的空间层次与阅读节奏。

远看具有强烈的视觉冲击和清晰的大形，近看能发现精致的材质、书法肌理、文化信息与图形细节。

整张海报应具有专业文博展览、艺术出版和文化品牌设计的完成度，成为一件具有独立主题表达的完整作品，而不是普通的器物展示模板。

确保器物造型准确、文字清晰、排版精密、色彩成熟。避免乱码、虚构展讯、无意义英文、廉价3D、过度科技特效、随机编号、四角星芒及水印。

最终输出一张9:16竖版高清艺术海报。

prompts.label: 完整提示词
prompts.text:
提示词：

【主题】：{青瓷 / 传统服饰 / 宣纸 / 砚石 / 其他东方文化材质}
【中文标题】：{4–6 字主题名称}
【英文标题】：{对应英文展览标题}
【核心主体】：{器物 / 织物 / 纸张 / 材质对象}
【辅助档案】：{线稿 / 古画 / 山水 / 结构图 / 材质研究 / 文献等}
【主色调】：{月白灰青 / 浅玉色 / 暖米灰 / 墨黑等}
【核心构图】：{景深留白 / 对角悬浮 / 纸层拼贴 / 大块材质裁切等}
【画幅比例】：9:16

设计一张高级东方文博编辑海报，将传统东方器物、织物、纸张或自然材质重新组织进当代博物馆展览、艺术出版物与文化研究视觉系统中。

整体视觉强调“克制、留白、材质与信息层级”，不是传统中国风装饰海报，也不是普通产品展示。

背景使用温润干净的暖象牙白、月白或极浅灰白艺术纸 / 展览空间，只保留极轻微真实纸张、织物或自然材质纹理，不做旧、不脏、不泛黄。

采用成熟的非对称编辑网格，让【核心主体】通过放大、裁切、悬浮、透光、虚焦、叠层、斜向进入或局部超出画面的方式参与构图。不要规整居中完整展示，而要让主体本身成为版式结构的一部分。

根据【核心构图】建立明确空间关系：

可使用前景虚化、中景主体、远景轮廓形成景深；
可使用半透明纸层、织物、玻璃或自然投影形成叠层；
可使用大块材质切面、留白和阴影形成抽象几何关系；
可让主体的轮廓、褶皱、边缘、孔洞、纹理或结构线自然参与文字排版。

Typography 使用现代宋体 / 明朝体与高对比 Serif 英文字体混排。

中文标题作为主要或次要视觉锚点，根据画面选择横排、竖排、错位或大尺度局部排列；英文标题承担另一层编辑层级。不要所有文字等大，要形成明显的“大标题 × 中型说明 × 极小档案信息”尺度差异。

在留白区域加入少量真正有意义的展览信息、材料研究、制作方式、文化说明和机构信息，使画面接近真实博物馆图录、艺术出版物或研究型展览视觉，而不是使用随机英文或 Lorem Ipsum。

加入与主题相关的【辅助档案】，例如：

器物轮廓线稿、山水档案、传统服饰结构图、材质截面、纸张纹理、拓片、手稿、器形分类、工艺研究图等。

所有辅助内容必须降低对比度、局部裁切、半透明化，只作为第二层或第三层信息，不与主体竞争。

色彩使用低饱和东方材质色，根据主题控制在 3–5 个主要色阶以内。例如：

暖象牙白 + 月白 + 灰青；暖米白 + 浅玉色 + 墨灰；暖白 + 淡茶褐 + 石灰；暖白 + 墨黑 + 浅石色。

不要为了“东方感”堆叠大量红、金、青绿等传统色。

画面必须建立清楚的三级观看关系：

远看：
主体大形、标题和留白首先成立，缩略图状态下仍然有明确视觉重心。

中距离：
能够发现材质、光影、景深、投影、裁切和主体与 Typography 之间的空间关系。

近距离：
才能阅读档案信息、研究标签、线稿、材质说明和细小文字。

保持约 45%–60% 的有效留白，但留白必须受到主体方向、光线、材质边界和文字网格的控制，不能只是单纯空着。

最终效果像亚洲顶级美术馆、设计博物馆、传统工艺研究机构或高级独立艺术出版物制作的东方文博展览主视觉：

传统对象经过当代编辑设计重新组织，安静、克制、真实、有空气感、有知识性，同时具有完整的作品感和成熟的信息层级。

避免：传统中国风模板、主体完整居中、商业产品广告、电商展示、红金配色堆叠、祥云边框、满屏书法、过度做旧、脏污纸张、CGI 塑料材质、强烈奢侈品高光、随机英文、信息过少、模板化极简、编号、No.、Vol.、四角星芒。

完整提示词
prompts.text:
prompt：https://promptsref.com/tool/AI-Image-Generator/share/a44a55037e5311d468467c3e1824866c

Create a highly realistic 3:4 vertical direct-flash portrait inside a dim late-night café or bakery. The subject is a clearly adult young woman with a slim, elongated upper-body silhouette, framed in a medium close-up to half-body crop from the head to around the waist. She has extremely long, straight honey-golden brown hair with slightly darker roots, a natural center part, substantial face-framing sections falling along the cheekbones and jaw, and the rest of the hair draping naturally over and behind her shoulders. Keep the hair smooth but unmistakably real, with minor flyaways, irregular strands, subtle messy ends and gentle golden-brown flash reflections rather than wig-like perfection.  Preserve the reference facial structure and proportions closely: face shape, eye spacing and shape, nose proportions, jawline and lip shape. Do not replace the face with a generic influencer template or overly slim the jaw. Use a lifestyle-oriented East Asian pop-idol / K-beauty soft-glam makeup direction: a thin luminous complexion base, softly defined light-brown brows, beige-pink-brown eyeshadow, fine black upper eyeliner extended slightly beyond the outer corners, separated long lashes and minimal lower-eye makeup. Her lips are naturally slightly parted and covered with glossy, wet-looking pink-nude lip color. She looks almost directly into the lens with a calm, soft, slightly detached expression, as though her attention has only just left the music. No smile.  Place oversized metallic silver-gray over-ear headphones on her head, with thick white ear cushions and a pale inner headband. Their large rounded oval earcups and metallic reflections should be visually prominent. This is not a mirror selfie and no phone should appear. Preserve the reference left-right arrangement instead of horizontally flipping it: the raised hand on the left side of the frame rests against the earcup on that same side, while the other hand holds a simple white takeaway coffee cup with a white lid lower in front of the torso.  She wears a fitted light heather-gray spaghetti-strap camisole with very thin straps and a faint silvery edge near the neckline. Over it is a visibly oversized powder-blue / pale cornflower-blue shirt-like lightweight jacket with long sleeves, loose accumulated folds and a small white embroidered letter-style emblem on one sleeve. The blue outer layer has slipped naturally off both shoulders, exposing the camisole straps, shoulders, collarbones and upper chest. Keep the fabric randomly wrinkled, slouchy and asymmetrical rather than perfectly arranged.  Visible skin includes the face, ear area, neck, collarbones, shoulders, upper chest, a small amount of upper-arm skin near the armhole, and both hands. Use a light neutral-warm beige skin tone that becomes slightly brighter beneath the flash while retaining subtle warmth. The skin should appear fine, soft and lightly moisturized—as though it would feel warm, supple and naturally smooth to the touch—while still retaining extremely subtle pores and real micro-texture. Do not use porcelain, waxy or completely airbrushed skin. The lips can appear considerably wetter and smoother than the skin.  Lighting is one of the most important identity features: use a strong, direct frontal flash positioned close to the camera axis, neutral to slightly cool white, fired from short range. Let it produce small specular highlights across the forehead, nose bridge, nose tip, cheeks, chin, collarbones and shoulder peaks, with additional sharp reflections on the metallic headphones and white cup lid. Permit slight highlight clipping in a few bright areas. Create short, physically believable shadows around the neck and shoulder transitions. The café itself should remain several stops darker with only a trace of weak warm ambient illumination. Do not add professional rim lighting, softboxes, side fill, beauty-dish lighting or elegant three-point illumination.  The camera should feel like a compact digital camera, point-and-shoot or casual phone photograph taken with a direct flash rather than a fashion-studio image. Use the perspective of roughly a 28–35mm full-frame-equivalent lens from close range. Keep the viewpoint almost at eye level but very slightly lower than the eyes. Position the subject a little left of center instead of using perfect symmetry, with extra dark environmental space on the right. Leave only a small amount of headroom.  Use moderate depth of field. The face, front hair, headphones, hands and cup should remain clearly readable, while the background becomes softer and much darker but is still recognizable. Do not create extreme creamy bokeh. Preserve genuine digital-camera texture: subtle shadow noise, mild JPEG softness, a touch of flash highlight overexposure, stray hairs, minor compression, uneven background detail, imperfect crop and small compositional offsets. Avoid hyper-sharp commercial retouching.  Behind her is a functioning late-night café, bakery or casual food-and-drink space rather than a photography set. Include a large dark glass window or glass partition with loose white handwritten bakery phrases scribbled across it; the writing only needs to look convincingly handwritten and does not need to be perfectly readable. Add dim, blurred seated patrons farther behind and toward the right, dark furniture, small interior reflections, a pale chair edge near the lower-right area and shadowy ceiling structures above. The environment should feel slightly cluttered, occupied and unstaged. Keep exploring the possibilities.

SYSTEM PROMPT: IMPERIAL VOID PROMPT COMPILER

ROLE

Convert the user's short image request, attached image, or combination of text and images into one finished image prompt.

Apply the Imperial Void visual system defined below. Do not explain the system. Do not reveal analysis. Do not add commentary. Return only the finished prompt.

Write the prompt in the user's language unless another language is requested.

If the user gives exact in-image text, preserve it exactly.

PRIMARY STYLE AIM

Create images that fuse refined East Asian architectural aesthetics with high-control minimalist composition.

The look combines:
- monumental negative space
- carved silhouette framing
- palace architecture with ornate rooflines
- scholar-painting atmosphere
- gongbi-like structural precision
- pale mineral landscape color
- sharp black and white field contrast
- elegant flowering branch forms
- editorial stillness
- museum-grade restraint

The image should feel quiet, elevated, intentional, and visually rare.

STYLE CORE

1. COMPOSITIONAL LOGIC
- Use dominant negative space as an active design element, not empty filler.
- Favor asymmetry with strong balance.
- Build the image around one major visual gesture.
- The main gesture may be:
  - a rock or void opening containing architecture and landscape
  - a flowering branch crossing the frame
  - a palace roofline intersecting a clean field
  - a monumental cutout, portal, or silhouette revealing an inner world
- Make the subject placement decisive and uncluttered.
- Avoid crowded layouts.
- Let the eye travel from a clear primary shape to smaller secondary details.

2. SPATIAL LANGUAGE
- Space should feel layered and vertical.
- Use depth through stacked terraces, pavilions, stairs, mountain ridges, distant halls, and receding architectural fragments.
- Keep background transitions soft and atmospheric.
- Use scale contrast:
  - tiny human figures
  - medium architectural masses
  - large enclosing silhouette or branch structure
- The image should feel larger than its frame.

3. ARCHITECTURAL DNA
- Architecture should draw from classical Chinese palace and garden architecture.
- Use:
  - sweeping tiled rooflines
  - painted bracket sets
  - red pillars
  - carved balustrades
  - stone stairs
  - layered pavilions
  - elevated terraces
  - courtyards and gateways
- Ornament should be precise but controlled.
- Detail density must be highest near focal architectural elements.

4. NATURAL MOTIFS
- Integrate natural elements with restraint.
- Preferred motifs:
  - plum blossoms or white blossoms
  - scholar rocks
  - pine forms
  - misty mountains
  - cliff faces
  - weathered branches
  - garden trees
- Natural forms should feel elegant and slightly stylized, not wild or chaotic.
- Branches should arc with calligraphic grace.

5. COLOR SYSTEM
Use a restrained palette.
Primary colors:
- ink black
- warm ivory
- parchment beige
- pale stone
- muted mineral blue
- oxidized blue-green
- weathered gold
- soft cinnabar red
- cedar brown
- cloud gray

Color handling rules:
- keep saturation controlled
- let one or two accent colors carry the image
- preserve tonal calm
- use black and white as structural anchors
- favor mineral and aged-pigment feeling over glossy digital color

6. SURFACE AND RENDERING
- The rendering should feel highly finished and crisp.
- Mix the refinement of traditional painted detail with modern graphic cleanliness.
- Edges should be selective:
  - architectural edges crisp
  - distant landscape edges softened
  - branch silhouettes clean
- Texture can suggest silk painting, mineral pigment, fine print, or archival paper, but should stay subtle.
- Avoid noisy over-texturing.

7. LIGHT
- Light should be soft, clear, and ceremonial.
- Favor diffused daylight, pale ambient glow, or calm spotlighting within darkness.
- The image may use strong contrast between void and illuminated subject.
- Avoid harsh cinematic rim lighting unless the image concept truly needs it.
- Lighting should clarify form and mood, not add spectacle for its own sake.

8. MOOD
- serene
- contemplative
- dignified
- timeless
- poetic
- slightly sacred
- still rather than dramatic

9. FIGURE TREATMENT
- If people appear, use them sparingly.
- Figures should often be small relative to architecture or space.
- Clothing can reference traditional robes or understated modern garments if requested.
- Poses should be quiet and readable.
- Do not crowd the scene with many active gestures.

10. DESIGN PRINCIPLES
- Every element must look curated.
- Favor visual silence over excess.
- Remove anything generic, flashy, or noisy.
- The image should feel like a luxury art print, exhibition poster, or collectible illustration rather than a random concept image.

SIGNATURE DEVICES

Use one or more of these when appropriate:
- a giant black void shape revealing an internal mountain-palace world
- a split black/white background with a branch or roofline crossing between the two halves
- tiny human figures at the base of monumental architecture
- a branch of white blossoms sweeping diagonally across a clean field
- a temple pavilion emerging from layered stone and mist
- elegant contrast between emptiness and ornament
- nested depth, where the viewer discovers smaller structures deeper inside the composition

SUBJECT ADAPTATION RULES

Portrait request:
- integrate the figure with architectural or floral framing
- use negative space and controlled ornament
- keep expression calm and noble

Landscape request:
- emphasize layered mountain architecture, terraces, and contemplative scale
- avoid generic postcard realism

Architecture request:
- prioritize roofline rhythm, pillar color, carved stair geometry, and atmospheric depth

Object or still life request:
- isolate the object against a strong field
- pair it with one elegant architectural or botanical counterpoint

Poster or cover request:
- keep layout clean
- leave intentional breathing room for typography if text is requested
- ensure the design remains striking at thumbnail scale

PROHIBITED DEFAULTS

Do not produce:
- cluttered scenes
- random fantasy clutter
- busy collage chaos
- neon cyberpunk treatment
- glossy 3D render look
- photobash mess
- generic anime look
- flat stock-photo composition
- heavy fog that obscures structure
- oversaturated colors
- excessive characters
- text unless requested
- decorative elements with no compositional purpose

PROMPT CONSTRUCTION METHOD

When writing the final prompt:
1. Identify the core subject from the user request.
2. Rebuild it through the Imperial Void visual system.
3. Specify the main compositional gesture first.
4. Define the spatial hierarchy.
5. Define the architecture, natural motifs, and palette.
6. Define the rendering, lighting, and mood.
7. Add any exact text or practical constraints from the user.
8. Keep the prompt specific, visual, and production-ready.

OUTPUT STANDARD

Return one finished image prompt only.
No bullets.
No analysis.
No labels.
No explanation.

【主题】：____

【主体器物 / 核心对象】：____
【聚核方式】：同心环抱 / 上下夹逼 / 双侧压缩 / 阵列围核

生成一张具有高级 Museum Editorial / Exhibition Poster 气质的「视觉聚核」海报。

先确定一个绝对视觉核心，再围绕它组织器物、文字、色块和留白。重点不是简单把主体放在画面中央，而是让其他视觉力量都把视线推向同一个核心。

根据主题选择一种聚核结构：

 同心环抱：利用圆形主体、文字、弧线或信息围绕核心形成向心关系。
 上下夹逼：用上下大色面、标题或留白向中部施压，把焦点锁定在主体。
 双侧压缩：左右 Typography、色块或信息区共同向中间收束，主体自身还可以利用框形轮廓形成二次聚焦。
 阵列围核：设置一个明显最大的主器，周围多个较小元素形成非对称围合；必须保持清楚的大小、疏密和主次关系。

主体承担主要视觉重量，其他元素只能“围绕、指向、托住或平衡”核心，不建立第二视觉中心。

Typography 参与构图：大中文标题负责视觉重量，小型英文、日期和机构信息集中在 1–2 个区域。避免把信息平均撒满版面。

色彩控制在 2–4 个主要颜色，通过大色块、器物材质和留白建立层级；保留足够负空间，不要为了丰富而堆叠装饰。

器物或主体使用真实、精致的博物馆藏品摄影 / 高质量对象摄影质感，材质、纹理、光影和阴影自然可信。

最终阅读顺序：
第一眼看到视觉核心 → 第二眼感受到周围元素向核心汇聚 → 第三眼阅读标题与辅助信息。

整体要求：聚焦明确、主次清晰、编辑感强、克制但有张力，具有成熟艺术机构、博物馆展览或高端文化海报的视觉品质。

避免：主体只是简单居中、元素平均分布、多个视觉中心、贴纸式散落、信息过量、装饰抢主体、电商详情页感、旅游文创感。

提示词：

展览名称：【填写展名】

主色调：【主色＋辅助色】
装饰纹样：【植物、几何、螺旋或其他主题纹样】
英文展名：【填写英文名称】
副标题：【填写展览主题】
展览日期：【填写日期】
展览地点：【填写场馆】

设计一张9:16竖版艺术展览海报，将克里姆特风格的装饰油画与日式美术馆编辑排版结合。只输出单张满版平面海报。

以原创成年人物半身肖像为主体，大幅放大并裁切头发、肩部与衣裙，让面孔在上半部形成清晰焦点。根据姿态安排偏左或偏右构图，为巨型标题留出空间。五官与颈肩结构自然，表情具有个性。

面部通过赭石、灰粉、暗红与冷灰色的小块油画笔触塑造，保留冷暖交错、底色露出和边缘虚实。面部笔触较细，头发、衣料与背景更自由，呈现艺术作品印刷复制的质感，避免摄影磨皮、光滑数字渐变和全图均匀的厚涂纹理。

服饰以所填主色形成宽阔、明确的大色块，少量衣褶交代体积，其余区域逐渐转为平面装饰。让所填纹样顺着肩背、衣袖或衣褶延伸，局部跨越人物轮廓，与背景融为一体。纹样大小错落、疏密有变化，面孔附近安静，衣裙与边缘区域丰富。

以黄赭、米黄、暗铜和黑褐色绘制哑金装饰，保留色层与细微颗粒。金色面积根据主色调调整：暖金主题可以满版，深蓝、绿色或绯红主题则保留集中色块。避免镜面金属、珠宝与立体浮雕效果。

将中文展名设计成具有构图作用的巨型文字，采用修长、粗细对比明显的明朝体或宋体。根据人物位置，选择沿边纵排或横竖错落的布局，直接叠印在头发、衣裙和背景上。允许少量非关键笔画贴边裁切，但主要字形完整、准确可辨，不遮挡眼睛、鼻子和嘴部。文字颜色以米白或深黑为主，与背景形成强烈明暗对比。

顶部排列细长的英文展名，底部直接叠印副标题、日期和场馆。建立巨型中文、中型日期、紧密小型展讯三个尺度，文字组共享清楚的对齐线，不另设独立底栏。保持丰富的展讯密度，同时确保文字清晰、日期与场馆完整处于画幅内。

整体让人物面部的体积、服饰背景的平面纹样与巨字排版相互配合。缩小观看时，仍能立刻识别面孔、主色块与展名。

仅使用填写的文字，不添加随机外文、虚构赞助商、编号、四角星芒、水印、画框或展示样机。若提供参考图，吸收其笔触、字体比例与信息密度，重新创作人物和纹样。

prompts.text:
提示词：

【主题】  
【四字中文标题】  
【主视觉材质】流体 / 柔性膜 / 熔融材料 / 颗粒 / 其他动态材料  
【物理变化】扩散 / 拉伸 / 熔化 / 振动 / 聚集 / 流动  
【背景主色】  
【字体主色】  
【强调色】  
【英文标题】  
【画面比例】9:16

生成一张具有 **East Asian Contemporary Exhibition Poster、Japanese Experimental Graphic Design、Editorial Art Direction、Corner-Pressure Composition** 气质的实验性竖版海报。核心使用“压角构图”：将【四字中文标题】拆成四个巨大汉字，从左上、右上、左下、右下向画面中心强势压入。四字不要等大、等距或形成四宫格，而是通过不同字号、裁切、出血量和进入中央的深度建立明显的向内压力。

画面中央设置一个体量足够大的【主视觉材质】，并通过【物理变化】形成与四角 Typography 相反或互相作用的视觉势能。重点不是“主体放在文字中间”，而是让材料本身真正参与版式：流体可以向外扩散并遮挡部分笔画；柔性膜可以被四角拉力撑开形成空间结构；熔融材料可以从固态逐渐软化、下坠并改变后方文字的视觉状态；颗粒可以因振动或物理作用自动聚集成具有规律的纹样。每张作品只选择一种最强的物理机制，避免同时堆叠过多特效。

主体必须具有真实、可信的材料属性和物理逻辑。例如流体需要有连续的浓度、卷吸和扩散关系；柔性材料需要有真实受力点、拉伸纹理、褶皱和接触阴影；熔融材料需要体现从固态、软化到流动的连续状态变化；颗粒必须具有真实粒径、密度变化、堆积与散落，而不是数字粒子特效。让观众明确感受到“材料正在运动、变形或响应外力”，而不是普通 3D 抽象造型。

Typography 分为三个层级：四角巨大中文字负责第一视觉；【英文标题】和中文作品名负责第二层；日期、地点、短句、材料关键词和少量说明负责第三层。使用明显字号反差、不对称对齐、局部竖排中文、紧凑英文和极细分隔线建立成熟的编辑设计感。信息密度保持中高，但不要平均铺满画面，应围绕主体形成局部密集区域，同时保留一部分干净负空间。

整体色彩控制在 3–4 个主要层级。【背景主色】作为大面积色域，【字体主色】建立稳定结构，【主视觉材质】承担最主要的形态与质感，【强调色】只用于极少量短线、日期节点、受力点或编辑标记。可以加入极轻纸张纹理、丝网印刷网点、胶印颗粒和局部套印感，但整体必须保持现代、干净、高级。

图文互动至少形成 2–3 处明确关系，例如主体从巨大字形前后穿过、在高密度区域使用反白文字、流体沿字形方向延伸、颗粒靠近笔画聚集、柔性材料真实遮挡部分汉字，或透明/半透明材料让后方文字产生自然视觉变化。所有互动都必须合理、可理解，并保证四个核心汉字仍然可辨认。

最终阅读顺序应为：第一眼看到四角巨字与中央动态主体形成的强烈大形；第二眼发现材料正在扩散、拉伸、熔化或振动；第三眼理解真实物理现象如何改变 Typography 和版面；最后阅读英文标题与少量展览信息。缩略图状态下必须具备明确焦点、强色彩对比和 Stop-scroll 冲击，放大后又能看到材料细节与精密编辑排版。

避免：机械四宫格、四字完全等大、主体过小、材料与字体彼此分离、普通抽象 3D Blob、液态金属滥用、数字粒子、随机烟雾、RGB glitch、赛博朋克、科技 HUD、复杂参数、无意义英文、Logo、二维码、编号、四角星芒和版权标识。

Prompt:

Create a bold editorial campaign poster where oversized typography reacts to a physical force created by the subject or product.

Brand: [BRAND NAME]
Product / Campaign: [PRODUCT OR CAMPAIGN]
Main Word: [SHORT WORD]
Subject: [PERSON / PRODUCT / BOTH]
Action: [STEP / JUMP / PULL / SKATE / ETC.]
Force: [PRESS / PUSH / WRAP / SLIDE / OTHER]
Force Direction: [DOWN / UP / ROTATE / DIAGONAL / OTHER]
Main Color: [COLOR]
Accent Color: [COLOR]
Aspect Ratio: [9:16]

Use realistic commercial photography, oversized typography, high-contrast colors, and contemporary editorial design.

Make the main word extremely large, filling roughly 50–75% of the frame. The typography should visibly respond to the chosen force instead of remaining static.

For example:

 PRESS: compress, bend, or shift the letters at the point of impact.
 PUSH: stretch the typography along an upward or forward direction.
 WRAP: let large letterforms pass behind and in front of the subject to create an enclosing motion.
 SLIDE: offset and shift the letters along one strong directional axis.

The deformation must follow the subject’s actual movement and force direction. Keep the typography graphic and readable — avoid turning it into soft 3D, liquid, or cartoon lettering.

Create clear foreground–subject–background interaction so the person or product feels physically connected to the type.

Use one dominant high-impact color with black, white, and a contrasting accent color. Add only a few meaningful campaign details such as the brand name, product name, slogan, specifications, labels, or small editorial text.

Keep people and products realistic, with believable proportions, materials, lighting, shadows, and dynamic movement.

The final image should feel like a finished campaign key visual where force, subject, typography, and composition all move together.

提示词：

【主题】：____  
【中文标题】：____  
【英文标题】：____  
【左侧视觉元素】：____  
【右侧视觉元素】：____  
【左右关系】：对望 / 围合 / 正反 / 交织 / 其他____  
【中轴内容】：灯幕 / 路径 / 针线 / 织物 / 留白 / 其他____  
【构图方式】：人物动作 / 轮廓夹景 / 空间透视 / 线性穿透 / 交织成形 / 其他____  
【主色调】：____  
【辅助色】：____  
【研究节点】：____  
【画面比例】：9:16  

生成一张具有强空间关系与成熟 Editorial Design 气质的「中轴夹景」文化海报。

先建立一个清楚的中央阅读区域，再让左右两侧元素通过真实关系共同形成中轴。两侧不只是做装饰性对称，而要真正参与主题表达。

可以根据题材选择不同关系：

人物对望：利用人物姿态、衣袖、操杆或视线共同夹出中央灯幕或焦点；

轮廓围合：利用伞面、建筑、器物或自然边缘围出雨巷、道路、天空等纵深空间；

正反穿透：使用同一对象的正反两面，并通过针、线、杆件等真实结构穿过中央，将两侧连接；

线性交织：让两组不同方向的线条在中央相遇，从独立线性元素逐渐形成完整织物、纹样或表面。

中轴不一定是一条色带，它可以是一块发光区域、一条纵深路径、一根真实针线、一段正在形成的织物，甚至是一块被两侧轮廓共同围出的负空间。

左右视觉重量保持平衡，但禁止机械镜像。可以通过颜色、姿态、材质、尺度和轮廓制造明显差异，只要两侧最终都把注意力推向中央。

Typography 根据每张主题重新设计，可横排、错位、跨区、贴近轮廓或与真实主体轻微穿插。不要固定使用四字纵排、中央巨大单字或同一种标题模板。

信息集中在 2–3 个区域，可加入一个面积约 5%–7% 的小型研究节点，例如动作轨迹、结构关系、针迹、开合状态或经纬组织，让画面更像成熟的文化展览视觉，而不是普通装饰海报。

色彩控制在 3–5 个主要颜色，优先使用明确的大色域和材质反差。

第一眼看到左右主体与中央关系；第二眼读到标题；第三眼发现人物、空间或线条究竟如何参与构图。

整体要求：高清、干净、结构明确、信息丰富但集中，具有 Museum Exhibition Poster × Contemporary Editorial Graphic Design × East Asian Cultural Visual 气质。

避免：机械镜像、左右元素没有真实关系、中央塞满无关信息、固定标题模板、多个视觉中心、随机装饰线、PPT 式信息框、过量小字、过度做旧、斑驳噪点和低完成度 AI 海报感。

The Functional Roles: for each component, infer its culinary role — base, filling, binder, garnish, sauce, seasoning, texture layer, aromatic element, structural shell, etc. The Visual Breakdown: determine how each component should be separately represented — whole ingredient, chopped form, bowl of prepared component, sauce sample, leaf, grain cluster, powder, slice, or texture sample. The Analytical Metrics: infer 1–2 simple explainer charts or diagrams per component, such as flavor profile, texture intensity, heat level, crunch factor, acidity balance, sweetness, richness, freshness, or aroma spectrum. The Scientific Overlay: generate plausible educational-style labels such as simplified chemistry notation, structural classification, ingredient family, preparation type, or culinary property markers — visually credible, not hardcoded. 2. The Immutable Container (The Clean Educational Poster): Goal: a modern food anatomy infographic board. white framed poster or mounted display board ultra-clean background central assembled food item in the middle surrounding ingredient callout boxes distributed symmetrically around the hero object thin connecting lines from each ingredient panel to the relevant part of the central food 3. The Poster Construction (Centerpiece + Callout System): Build the poster as a structured educational layout: a large bold title at the top generated from Input A in the format of an anatomy / breakdown / composition study one central high-quality rendered image of Input A 4–8 surrounding ingredient boxes, each containing: a clean visual of one inferred component the component name one short scientific / pseudo-technical notation line one or two small chart graphics or profile diagrams color-code the component boxes subtly according to ingredient category if appropriate 4. No Hardcoding Constraint: Do not assume taco ingredients, sandwich ingredients, or any fixed food structure. Instead: if Input A is layered, infer layers if Input A is wrapped, infer shell + filling system if Input A is plated, infer sauce + protein + garnish + base if Input A is a beverage, infer liquid phases, toppings, foam, ice, aromatics, or inclusions if Input A is a dessert, infer crust, filling, glaze, texture contrast, decoration, and flavor accents if Input A is simple, infer fewer but more essential components The infographic must be generated from the variable food item itself. 5. Educational Graphic Style: The board should feel like a hybrid of: culinary science poster museum food explainer modern menu lab graphic clean commercial infographic Use: bold sans-serif typography neat line connectors minimalist charts clean color accents organized spacing and strong readability 6. Visual Syntax & Atmosphere: Camera: straight-on poster view, orthographic or near-orthographic Lighting: bright, soft, shadow-controlled studio lighting Background: clean tiled wall, neutral interior, or pure white presentation space Detail: premium food-render realism in the central item and ingredient samples Aesthetic: educational, appetizing, precise, modern, and visually balanced 7. Output Constraint: The final image should work for any Input A: tacos ramen croissants burgers sushi salad bowls dumplings bubble tea pizza pastries curries sandwiches All labels, component choices, and charts must be inferred from the variable dish, with no hardcoded ingredient set. Output: ONE image, square aspect ratio, clean framed educational food anatomy poster for Input A, featuring a central hero dish, AI-inferred ingredient callout panels, minimalist data charts, labeled connectors, and no hardcoded subject details.

1/ Character sheets + storyboard

Create two original East Asian fantasy fighters who were once two halves of the same soul. Keep a similar facial structure, but give them opposite visual identities.

Character A:
Elegant and controlled, amber eyes, long dark hair with one braid, layered teal and gray-blue robes, aged bronze ring weapons releasing thin cyan-gold fate threads.

Character B:
Sharp and rebellious, red eyes, short black wolf-cut hair with one braid, asymmetrical cinnabar-red and bone-white battle robes, a black-gold curved chain blade.

Create detailed full-body character sheets with front, side and back views, facial close-ups, costume materials and weapon details.

Then create a 16:9 pencil action storyboard with 16 tightly arranged panels and minimal gaps.

Show close-ups, vertical drops, wrist kicks, knockbacks, chain-assisted re-entry, leg traps, curtain impacts, corridor chases, weapon locks, roof crashes and a final wide shot.

Use extreme perspective, low angles, weapon POV, over-the-shoulder tracking and partial-body framing.

Clear attack → reaction → recoil → re-entry.

Monochrome graphite pencil sketches, rough animation keyframes, motion lines, impact marks and English labels only.

2/ Seedance prompt

15-second, 16:9, high-energy hand-drawn anime fight with fluid Sakuga-style motion.

Use the character sheets to lock both fighters’ faces, costumes, proportions and weapons. Use the storyboard to guide key poses, combat flow, screen direction and camera movement.

Motion Phrase 1
The red fighter cuts the main fate thread. The teal fighter drops from the upper beams and kicks her weapon hand, sending her sliding across the wooden stage.

Motion Phrase 2
The red fighter anchors her chain blade into a beam and pulls herself back like a projectile. She traps the teal fighter’s leg and throws her through several hanging curtains.

Motion Phrase 3
A fast chase through a narrow corridor. The teal fighter releases one anchored thread and uses the remaining tension to change direction. The incoming strike misses, followed by a counterattack from behind and a close-range weapon lock.

Motion Phrase 4
Both fighters pull against the chain and fate threads until the force explodes. They are launched in opposite directions, crash onto the wet roof and immediately re-enter the fight. End with a glowing soul-thread revealed between them as the opera house collapses into the storm.

The camera follows the current attacker’s momentum through extreme close-ups, low tracking, weapon POV, whip pans, falling follow shots and short 90–120° orbits during close contact.

Avoid static two-shots, repeated symmetrical compositions, stationary spellcasting, random cuts and long 360° camera orbits.

Build one consistent visual identity across all pages, with the same character proportions, facial features, signature accessories, color system, typography, materials, and proposal layout. Use a premium editorial case-study style with a small brand lockup, irregular dark chapter tab, slim vertical navigation, asymmetric footer, controlled whitespace, fine annotations, and subtle cut / fold geometry. Page 1 — Character Identity

The environment should feel like a natural extension of the character rather than an unrelated backdrop.

Page 4 — Extensions & Packaging
Create several clearly different character variations based on specific tasks, tools, outfits, or use cases while keeping the core identity unchanged. Add one premium collectible packaging or product application and a small extension-logic diagram showing how the character can scale into a commercial IP system.

Across all pages, vary the internal composition instead of repeating the same grid. Use large, medium, small, and micro visual scales to create rhythm. Let sketches, 3D renders, annotations, close-ups, materials, and product applications work together as design evidence.

Create a sophisticated vertical editorial poster built around a clear three-part composition: top, middle, and bottom.

Each section must have a distinct visual role, but the final poster should feel like one continuous design rather than three stacked rectangular panels.

Use strong differences in scale, image density, typography, and negative space to establish hierarchy.

The top section should create the first visual anchor through a bold image, oversized typography, or a strong subject.

The middle section should act as the structural hinge of the composition. It can use a title, information field, narrow panoramic image, color band, or typography layer to connect the upper and lower sections.

The bottom section should provide a second visual weight or spatial conclusion through a landscape, object, secondary portrait, or oversized type.

Avoid rigid card-like boundaries. Let selected elements cross between sections through masking, overlap, irregular silhouettes, transparency, atmospheric transitions, foreground/background relationships, or typography extending beyond its original area.

Typography must actively participate in the composition rather than simply sit on top of the image. Allow large letterforms to be cropped by the page, partially hidden behind subjects, overlap imagery, or interact with negative space.

Use a strong editorial hierarchy:
one dominant title,
one clear secondary information layer,
and small meaningful metadata such as dates, venue, category, or curatorial text.

Small text should feel like real exhibition or editorial information, not decorative filler.

Keep some areas intentionally quiet. Do not fill every empty space.

The first read should communicate the main visual structure immediately.
The second read should reveal the interaction between type and imagery.
The third read should reveal the smaller information and details.

Maintain a refined contemporary poster aesthetic with strong typography, deliberate cropping, controlled information density, clean print texture, and professional editorial spacing.

生成一张具有强设计感的曲线构图海报，整体采用 Contemporary Editorial Poster × Postmodern Graphic Design × Cultural Exhibition Poster 的视觉语言。

先确定一条最重要的主曲线，再围绕它组织主体、Typography、图片、信息和留白。曲线不是装饰，而是整张海报的视觉骨架与阅读路径。

根据内容选择一种主要曲线方式：

曲线大字：让大型 Typography 本身发生拉伸、弯折、裁切和出框，字形直接成为曲线主视觉。

曲面翻折：让纸张、织物、建筑面或其他可弯曲实体形成巨大曲面，并把文字、图片和信息直接放在曲面上，随透视自然弯曲。

螺旋拼贴：用一条开放式螺旋路径串联照片、票据、文字、人物和小型视觉节点，从外围逐渐引导到核心。

曲线串联：用一条连续 S 型或弧形主线穿过多个不同尺度的视觉节点，让原本分散的图片、人物和文字形成完整叙事。

整张海报只保留一个最强曲线方向，其他线条和元素只能跟随或平衡主曲线，不制造新的视觉竞争。

主标题必须参与构图，可顺着曲线错位、跨区、裁切、局部遮挡或改变尺度，不要只是整齐放在顶部。

画面允许摄影、插画、手写、色块、纸张、票据等 2–3 种视觉语言发生碰撞，但所有素材必须围绕同一条曲线路径组织，避免随机贴纸式拼贴。

控制明显的视觉层级：第一眼看到主曲线和主视觉；第二眼看到大标题；第三眼沿曲线路径阅读图片和信息；最后才看到日期、地点和极小辅助文字。

保留大面积有效留白，允许不对称、裁切、尺度失衡、局部出框和轻微套色偏移，让版式具有松动但有秩序的后现代编辑设计感。

色彩控制在 3–5 种，以一个大面积主色、一个强对比色和少量点缀色建立识别度。

整体要求：曲线明确、视觉抓眼、信息丰富但不杂乱、有人工排版感、有设计学院和艺术出版物气质。

Create a realistic outdoor casual cosplay / futuristic sportswear portrait of an unmistakably adult young woman seated astride a bicycle. She has a short creamy platinum-blonde curled bob, softly voluminous at the crown, with airy broken bangs and loose curled ends around the jaw and upper neck. Her face should remain softly rounded with a natural jawline rather than an exaggerated V-shaped influencer face. Use understated makeup inspired by Japanese cosplay and East Asian fashion portraiture: pale pink mid-face blush, muted pink-brown eyeshadow, fine delicate eyeliner, moderate lashes, and soft dusty-rose lips. Her complexion is fair with a subtle natural pink undertone and real tonal variation.  Her head is tilted slightly backward, her eyes half-open and gently narrowed, looking near or just past the camera. Her lips remain naturally closed with no deliberate smile. The expression is calm, languid, self-possessed and slightly detached. She had just stopped the bicycle; one hand is still gripping the collar or edge of the zipper near her chest while the other lightly holds the lower front hem of the top. The shutter caught that brief pause, and she now looks as though she may return her hand to the handlebars and ride away a second later.  She wears a very pale icy-blue fitted long-sleeve technical sports top with futuristic cycling-wear cues. The long central zipper is opened deeply, creating a strong vertical V-shaped front opening while clothing coverage remains intact, with a pale under-bust garment band visible underneath. The sleeves have fine breathable mesh or perforated texture, with two tiny teal geometric marks on the upper chest and a few subtle gray bars on one arm. The fabric should stretch naturally over the body while retaining small realistic folds, tension lines and distortions instead of looking like perfect 3D cloth simulation. Pair it with light gray-white high-waisted fitted cycling shorts made of matte stretch fabric, naturally pulled around the hips and thighs by the seated riding position.  Visible skin includes the face, neck, central upper chest below the collarbones, a small amount of torso inside the opened zipper, both hands and the thighs below the cycling-short hems. Skin should be fair with a mild pink undertone, soft and fine, mostly matte with a faint satin surface. It should visually suggest smooth human skin that would feel soft to the touch, while preserving subtle pores, tiny tonal variations and believable softness rather than plastic perfection.  Photograph from a distinctly low angle, with the camera approximately at bicycle-handlebar or hip height and tilted upward. Add a subtle Dutch tilt and do not perfectly correct the horizon. Use the perspective of roughly a 35–40mm full-frame equivalent environmental portrait lens, with 35–50mm acceptable, and an aperture feel around f/2 to f/2.8. Frame it as a medium-full / three-quarter portrait, cropped from around the lower thighs upward. The subject fills most of the vertical image, with her head near the upper-right area.  A black bicycle handlebar and brake assembly should cross strongly through the lower foreground and remain slightly out of focus. Include another pale bicycle component blurred in the lower-left corner so that the foreground partially obstructs the body and gives the photograph genuine depth rather than a perfectly clean fashion composition.  The location is an ordinary outdoor courtyard, event area or roadside space beside an older building, not a studio set. Fill the left side with a large green tree canopy. Behind her, include aged red doors or wall panels, muted brick-red surfaces and gray concrete structures, with a few small colorful objects near ground level. The upper and right side of the frame should open into a large bright overcast sky that is close to white clipping. Keep a little real-world clutter, suggesting an outdoor cosplay event, cycling gathering, backstage zone or older urban courtyard.  Light the entire scene only with natural overcast daylight. The huge bright sky acts like an enormous softbox overhead, slightly stronger from camera-right, softly lifting the right side of the face, platinum hair, upper torso and thighs. Let environmental bounce fill the opposite side. Keep broad soft highlights, gentle occlusion beneath the nose and jaw and around clothing edges, with no hard flash, no aggressive rim light and no obvious three-point studio lighting. Allow the white sky to overexpose slightly.  The final image should feel moderately soft rather than commercially razor-sharp, with a little digital denoising, gentle diffusion and natural optical blur. Keep the face and upper body reasonably clear while the trees, architecture and distant objects fall softly out of focus; the closest handlebars should also be slightly blurred. Preserve photographic imperfections: imperfect horizon, slightly off-center framing, foreground obstruction, clipped sky, garment wrinkles, miscellaneous background clutter and subtle digital noise.  The emotional tone is quiet, confident, mildly languid and slightly distant: close physical camera distance combined with emotional restraint. It should feel like a real photographer caught a distinctive moment at an outdoor event rather than a perfectly engineered commercial shoot.  Negative prompt: underage, anime render, 3D CGI, plastic skin, over-retouched skin, extreme hourglass, oversized anatomy, transparent clothing, explicit nudity, hard flash, studio rim light, perfect symmetry, centered passport composition, hyper-sharp HDR, extra fingers, warped hands, warped bicycle, duplicate limbs, heavy glamour makeup, watermark, text.

prompts.text:
提示词：

【主题】：
【中文标题】：
【英文标题】：
【核心主体】：
【左右关系】：巨物压场 / 图像窄带 × 宽文字场 / 主体 × 档案 / 图像越界 / 密集 × 留白 / 其他
【左侧内容】：
【右侧内容】：
【跨界元素】：器物轮廓 / 枝叶 / 大字 / 线稿 / 纹样 / 其他
【主色调】：
【强调色】：
【日期 / 场馆】：
【画面比例】：9:16

生成一张高审美、高信息密度的东方文化展览海报，采用「左右构图 / 非对称双区构图」。

左右不要 50 / 50 平均切开，根据主体体量、文字密度和留白关系灵活使用 35 / 65、40 / 60、45 / 55 等比例。重点不是两侧面积相等，而是让图像重量、Typography 和信息密度达到视觉平衡。

根据主题灵活选择不同方式：

巨物压场：一侧放大尺度器物、文物或艺术对象，允许大胆裁切，占据主要视觉重量；另一侧通过标题、英文、小字、结构线稿和展讯建立阅读层级。

图像窄带 × 宽文字场：一侧使用修长古画、摄影或纹样切片，另一侧保留更大的纸面与 Typography。图像中的枝叶、飞鸟、云气或主体轮廓可主动越出画芯进入文字区。

主体 × 档案：一侧保持单一强主体，另一侧组合器型线稿、材质微距、拓片、纹样研究、尺寸、年代和少量说明文字，形成艺术图录感。

密集 × 留白：一侧通过图像、档案碎片和研究内容形成高密度视觉，另一侧保持大面积控制过的留白，只使用少量大字和关键展讯。留白不能只是“没有内容”，要通过字距、细线、位置和比例被精确设计。

左右边界不要过于机械。可以让器物边缘、大字、花枝、纹样或研究线条跨过分界约 3%–10%，把两侧重新连接起来，但避免随意拼贴。

Typography 必须根据每张画面的主体重新设计。可以使用超大单字、两字错位、完整横排标题、中等尺度标题、跨栏文字或局部反色。坚持“大字很大、小字很小”的尺度反差，减少无意义的中号字。不要固定使用四字纵排，也不要重复“两字横排 + 两字竖排”的模板。

信息密度参考成熟博物馆海报、Japanese Editorial Design 和 Art Catalogue。可加入英文副标题、年代、材质、工艺、场馆、日期、策展短句，以及 1–3 个与主题直接相关的研究节点，例如器型线稿、釉面微距、古画材料、纹样拓片、石纹研究或局部放大。

这些辅助信息必须服务主题，不要为了“显得专业”而堆随机小字。

色彩控制在 3–5 个主要颜色。优先使用骨白、墨黑、青瓷绿、石青石绿、深灰、赭色等克制色彩，再加入一个明确但面积很小的朱砂红或其他强调色。纸面保持干净，不使用脏黄仿古滤镜。

第一眼看到大型主体与左右重量关系；第二眼看到标题和主要色块；第三眼发现器物、古画或枝叶如何突破左右边界；最后再阅读材质、结构、年代与展览档案。

核心原则：一边负责压住视觉，一边负责承接阅读；留白也是重量，信息密度也是重量；左右不相等，但整体必须平衡。

整体要求：9:16，高清、清晰、纸面干净、主体质感真实、Typography 锐利、细线与小字尽可能清楚，信息丰富但不乱，具有成熟博物馆海报和艺术出版物完成度。

避免：机械五五分、简单左图右字、左右各放一个相似主体、主体过小、信息区像说明书、固定标题模板、PPT 信息框、复杂 UI、随机英文、严重做旧、斑驳噪点、画面编号、版权标识、四角星芒、sparkle 和低完成度 AI 海报感。

prompt：https://promptsref.com/tool/AI-Image-Generator/share/0d0ed261c3bb9109fa63680dd457cf35
Create a **9:16 vertical, clean photographic image with absolutely no interface or text overlays**. An adult woman in her 20s is seated on a pale floor at the base of a rough gray-white plaster wall. Her torso leans slightly backward toward the wall, with one hand planted on the floor just behind and beside her body for support. She has natural black medium-long to long hair, loosely side-parted and disturbed by a light breeze; some strands touch the wall while others lift irregularly around her head. Keep small flyaway hairs, slight frizz and believable disorder instead of polished commercial hair styling.  She wears a fitted black lace spaghetti-strap camisole or lingerie-inspired top with a subtle scalloped lace edge. An oversized black shirt or lightweight jacket is loosely draped around her, slipping off the shoulders and naturally pooling around her arms and sides. Pair it with black fitted bottoms, deep-red semi-sheer thigh-high stockings with a darker red upper welt, and vivid red patent pointed or narrow-toed stiletto heels. The hosiery must remain genuinely semi-transparent so the warm skin tone is still visible underneath the red material; do not turn the stockings into opaque leggings.  Keep the pose noticeably asymmetrical and slightly accidental. One leg is bent upward with the knee extremely close to the camera, occupying a large central-lower portion of the foreground and appearing larger because of wide-angle perspective. The other leg bends and then extends diagonally toward the lower-right edge, naturally approaching or even slightly leaving the frame. Do not square the torso or shoulders perfectly. Preserve a mild body twist, realistic weight distribution and believable muscular tension, as though she had been adjusting her posture a second ago and has only now briefly become still.  Place her face in the upper half of the composition. Her eyes are slightly heavy-lidded and directed toward the low-positioned camera, carrying a calm, cool and faintly tired expression. Her lips remain naturally closed or softly relaxed, with no deliberate smile. Preserve natural facial proportions and subtle asymmetry. Use a restrained East Asian fashion-editorial makeup direction: clean semi-matte complexion, naturally elongated brows, thin dark brown-black eyeliner extending slightly outward, separated lashes without oversized falsies, subtle under-eye definition, and muted rose-brown or dusty red lips. Avoid heavy Western-style contouring.  Visible skin includes the face, neck, shoulders, collarbones and upper-chest edge, both arms and hands, and a narrow area of upper thigh/hip above the stocking welt. Use a light to light-medium warm complexion with gentle peach-beige undertones. Skin should look refined but genuinely human rather than airbrushed: visually warm, soft and slightly velvety to the touch, with subtle pores, natural color variation around joints and realistic surface contours.  Photograph the scene as though a friend captured a spontaneous smartphone frame from close range, not as a professional studio campaign. Use approximately a **24–28mm full-frame-equivalent wide-angle perspective**. Position the camera close to seated leg height, clearly below her eyes, and angle it slightly upward. This should exaggerate the raised knee and foreground legs through perspective while allowing the face to appear comparatively smaller. Use moderate smartphone-style depth of field: the face, torso and much of the foreground legs remain readable, while the rough wall texture is still clearly visible. Avoid exaggerated creamy bokeh.  Illuminate the subject mainly with a single warm directional source entering from frame-right or front-right, resembling late-afternoon window light or warm ambient side light. Let it strike the right side of her cheek, shoulder, upper-chest edge and legs, producing soft highlights that gradually fall into shadow. The side close to the wall, the black outer garment and the opposite side of the body remain naturally darker. Let the right half of the wall become slightly brighter so its uneven plaster creates many tiny highlight-and-shadow variations. Do not add ring-light catchlights, obvious rim lighting, perfect fill light or a conventional three-point studio setup.  Maintain a strong red, black and pale-gray color relationship. The overall mood is cool, languid and quiet, carrying the remaining warmth of a moment just before night. It should feel like a real frame pulled from a casual smartphone video: the hair is still moving, the composition is slightly offset, legs and shoes approach the edges, the wall and floor can contain small authentic marks or scuffs, and the image retains subtle smartphone noise, compression character and mild computational sharpening. Avoid polished commercial perfection.  **Remove every element belonging to the original social-media screenshot.** No top status bar, clock, battery icon, 5G or Wi-Fi indicator, menu, search icon, like/comment/favorite/share buttons, profile avatar, follow button, username, captions, hashtags, music bar, bottom navigation, platform watermark, logo, text overlay or any other app-interface component. The final image must read purely as a clean photograph, never as a screenshot.  Negative prompt: UI, app interface, status bar, icons, text overlay, subtitle, username, watermark, logo, like button, comment button, share button, navigation bar, phone in hand, mirror selfie, ring light, commercial studio glamour, plastic skin, over-retouched skin, extreme body proportions, extra limbs, deformed hands, opaque red leggings, heavy bokeh, perfect symmetry.

prompts.text:
Keep exploring the possibilities.

SYSTEM PROMPT: PAINTERLY ANIMATED THRILLER DIRECTOR

TARGET
Midjourney V8.2

FUNCTION

Write original image prompts for painterly animated film stills. Handle portraits, dialogue, action, environments and connected stories. Use urban suspense as the default direction, not a compulsory plot. Adapt the same rendering to other settings and genres when requested.

Build dimensional faces, bodies and environments with painted color planes, visible brushwork and selective drawn details. Preserve volume beneath the paint. Do not produce photographs with paint filters, smooth plastic renders or flat vector illustrations.

Work with or without references, moodboards and personalization. Follow the user's subject, cast, age, setting, tone, image count, ratio and output format. Do not depend on another user's account or project.

DEFAULTS

Aspect ratio: 16:9.
Image count: one unless otherwise requested.
Sequence length: five when a sequence is requested without a count.
Human lead: one original adult suited to the brief.
Setting: contemporary urban space when unspecified.
Tone: suspense through action, distance and visibility.
Violence: non-graphic unless specified otherwise.

Do not impose a gender, ethnicity, occupation, haircut or costume. The black-haired woman in a coral jacket is an example, not a required identity. Independently generated frames can still form one connected story.

REFERENCES

Apply current instructions, approved project decisions, references within their assigned roles, then defaults.

Separate style, identity, costume, pose, composition and lighting references. Extract rendering from a style image without copying its face, clothes or scene.

Separate illustrations from captions, borders, parameter strips and letterboxing. A collage supplies examples, not permission for a split-screen output. Written camera labels are authored directions, not measured properties of the image. Resolve conflicting viewpoints instead of combining them.

Analyze only available material. Do not invent unseen images, account settings, URLs or reference codes. Without references, describe the necessary rendering in words.

FORM AND BRUSHWORK

Construct the face, torso, hands and architecture as volumes. Use painted tonal changes, overlap and light to explain their planes. Keep facial features structurally related through turns and expressions.

Place broad paint patches on cheeks, garments and walls, finer marks near eyes and hands, and looser strokes in distant scenery. Follow the surface: cheek planes, sleeve bends, concrete edges and movement direction.

Use selective pencil-like contours around eyelids, hair separations, folds, rails and worn edges. Avoid uniform outlines and equally sized scratches across every material.

Keep firm edges at the important eye, hand or contact point. Break edges along cloth and hair; soften distant forms. Angular painted shadows may coexist with restrained soft transitions. Do not flatten every face into two tones or smooth away all brushwork.

Paint must describe structure rather than sit over photographic detail. Avoid all-over canvas texture, heavy impasto and uniform grain. Describe a finished animated frame rather than a painting photographed on a board.

DETAIL AND MATERIALS

Give the clearest detail to the principal expression, supporting hand or decisive contact. Simplify distant windows, traffic and buildings into grouped shapes while preserving routes and scale.

Skin uses painted tonal patches, limited highlights and expression lines, not photographic pores or cosmetic retouching. Preserve facial depth without waxy shine.

Hair forms opaque masses with drawn separations and selected loose strands. Do not reveal hidden features through solid hair. Retain the established cut.

Clothing uses broad fold planes, tension, creased sleeves and selective highlights. Seams and fastenings follow construction. Concrete and plaster use worn patches and chipped edges where contact or exposure explains them. Metal retains recognizable structure beneath restrained highlights and wear.

Keep skin, cloth, concrete, metal and glass distinct. Painterly treatment does not turn every surface into rough fabric. Do not blur the decisive eye, hand or landing merely to imitate shallow focus.

COLOR AND LIGHT

The default relationship uses a coral-red focal garment or object, pale mint illumination or environmental color, dusty peach surfaces and charcoal shadows. Assign each role to a specific object or source. Do not apply a uniform color wash.

Keep coral concentrated near the focal subject, with smaller or quieter background echoes. Mint may belong to fluorescent light, sky fill, paint or glass reflections; it must not make every face green. Preserve local skin color beneath reflected light.

Attach colors directly to their nouns: coral-red jacket, charcoal trousers, dusty peach wall, pale mint fluorescent tube. Do not append detached palette lists. A warm reflection on black hair does not change its local color.

When the user supplies another palette, preserve focal separation and readable shadows rather than forcing coral and mint. Maintain color ownership across characters and frames.

Choose a dominant motivated source, such as daylight through a light well, a fluorescent fitting, storefront light or dawn. Secondary illumination requires a source or reflecting surface. Avoid automatic contrasting rim lights, neon, rain and wet asphalt.

Retain shape within charcoal shadows without lifting the entire scene into gray haze. Light must support the expression and spatial relationship. Do not add beams or atmospheric particles without environmental justification.

CHARACTER AND PERFORMANCE

Define age, build, facial proportions, eyes, brows, nose, mouth, hair mass and costume silhouette. Use a few identifying traits rather than an anatomical inventory. Expressive eyes must remain compatible with the requested age; do not default to doll-like adult faces.

Keep a full internal identity specification and repeat its visible essentials in each prompt. Names and phrases such as same character do not replace self-contained descriptions.

Close-ups prioritize face and expression. Medium shots add hands and interaction. Wide shots prioritize silhouette, clothing color, posture and direction. Omit details outside the frame.

Choose one principal reaction. Describe eyelids, mouth tension, a raised inner brow, interrupted gesture or altered grip. Do not stack conflicting emotions or make every reaction a scream.

Direct the gaze toward a specific person, reflection, object or route. A turning head may leave the shoulders facing the previous direction, but the eyes cannot follow two unrelated targets at once. Eye contact with the camera needs a scene-based reason unless a direct portrait is requested.

Give the character decisions as well as reactions. Do not make every adult woman a frightened courier followed by a stranger. Clothing and equipment should reflect the task, weather and movement.

ACTION AND MOTION

For action, establish support, weight-bearing limb, direction, obstacle and immediate destination. Heavy objects affect posture. Hands must grip, push, support, release or reach toward something specific.

A turn shows changed footing, torso rotation and trailing cloth. A vault shows contact, clearance and a receiving surface. Stair movement connects feet, landing and railing. Airborne action needs a readable takeoff or destination.

Use foreshortening to explain depth and force. Keep the foreground arm connected to its shoulder and the hand recognizable. Do not enlarge a limb without a compatible near-camera position.

Choose one instant. Do not combine approaching, gripping, releasing and landing in one image.

Confine painted motion accents to moving hair tips, fabric, limbs or receding scenery. Keep the main expression and decisive support readable. Avoid duplicated faces, extra fingers, full-body ghosting and uniform motion blur. Still scenes need no speed marks.

CAMERA AND BLOCKING

State camera height, distance and direction before adding an optional focal-length cue. Use one compatible viewpoint. A 24mm to 28mm cue can support near wide-angle action; a 35mm to 50mm cue can support less expanded observational framing. These are choices, not mandatory settings or measurements of references.

Do not label an overhead view low-angle or combine a frontal face with the back of the head. Use architectural convergence to explain height and confinement while retaining usable structures.

Foreground seats, doors, railings and laundry may partially restrict the view. Preserve the decisive gesture unless concealment is intentional. Close-up cropping must retain the features needed for the reaction.

In wide shots, keep the protagonist readable through posture and costume rather than reducing them to an anonymous dot. Distant secondary people may remain simplified silhouettes when their presence is the clue.

For two or more characters, assign screen position, depth, action and gaze to each. Use opposing profiles, over-the-shoulder framing or staggered depth as the interaction requires. Do not force everyone into front-facing, equally lit positions.

Preserve eyelines and the action axis. Distinguish anatomical left and right from screen-left and screen-right. Do not exchange clothing, props or injuries between characters when the camera moves.

URBAN GEOGRAPHY

Build usable streets, corridors, light wells, bridges, platforms, stairwells and vehicle interiors. Doors and stairs must connect to accessible spaces. A route leads somewhere; an obstruction occupies a visible location.

Group windows, air-conditioning units, pipes and cables into architectural masses. Detail should explain scale, habitation or access rather than compete with the protagonist.

Place wear and belongings where use supports them. Do not turn every neighborhood into decorative rubble or an automatic dystopia. Preserve requested cultural and geographic context without inferring a named city from architectural shorthand.

Let ordinary construction affect the scene: a curtain restricts visibility, a taxi frame limits a view, a closed door stops movement. Supernatural events are optional. Do not invent an exit at the ending solely to resolve a chase.

GLASS AND REFLECTIONS

Establish the glass plane, camera side, character side, transmitted view and reflected space. Decide which layer carries the clue; reduce competing contrast in the others.

Keep reflected anatomy, hair and gestures consistent with the actual person. A reflection is not an independent duplicate. A separate reflected person requires a plausible position in the scene.

Specify whether a hand touches the pane or stops short. At contact, the palm rests against the surface rather than passing through it.

Use selected droplets, streaks and bright brush marks for wet glass. Keep reflections on the pane and distinct from motion smears. Impossible reflections require an explicitly supernatural brief, not an accidental mismatch.

SHOT OPTIONS

Select according to the current event. Do not cycle through these mechanically or copy the reference scenes.

ENCLOSED WINDOW
Use a seat, door or frame to compress the view. Establish the gaze target and distinguish reflection from exterior scenery. Keep the face and relevant hand readable.

THRESHOLD PAUSE
Show interrupted movement at an entrance. Choose hovering, touching, pulling or withdrawing. The door, posture and visible interior explain access and hesitation.

CORNER TURN
Show the body redirecting around an obstacle, with support and trailing cloth. Choose a backward glance or attention to the new route, not both.

BARRIER CROSSING
Show the barrier, planted hand, clearance and destination. Use surrounding height to establish stakes without sacrificing a plausible landing.

CITY GAP
Place the protagonist on a defined support with the next route visible. Preserve readable posture and simplify distant architecture.

OBSTRUCTED SIGHTLINE
Frame a foreground reaction looking toward a distant person. Establish what separates them. Keep ambiguity in intention, not broken geography.

REACTION CLOSE-UP
Isolate recognition or an interrupted turn. Use painted facial planes, drawn eyelids and a simplified background rather than photographic skin or glamour posing.

STAIRWELL DEPTH
Expose connected flights and landings from one chosen direction. Give each person a plausible level and support. Keep railings from intersecting bodies.

STORY AND CONTINUITY

For connected images, establish one objective, obstacle, usable route, available resources, consequential decision and resulting state. Keep planning internal unless requested.

Retain the requested protagonist throughout. A five-frame story about one woman must not become five unrelated women or five demonstrations of different techniques.

Each frame changes information, position, access, trust, condition or available options. Establish objects and dangers before they determine the outcome. Keep clues readable at the chosen scale rather than dependent on tiny writing or invisible backstory.

Vary intensity according to events. Movement can lead to stillness. Do not default to reflection reveals, rooftop escapes or sunrise endings. Motives may remain ambiguous while the physical event remains understandable.

Track face, hair, clothing, footwear, equipment, injuries, wetness, fatigue, damage, location, screen direction and lighting. Preserve object ownership, garment construction and established landmarks. Changes require causes and plausible elapsed time.

Use the same rendering language across the sequence. Close shots may carry finer marks and action shots stronger smears, but neither becomes live-action photography or flat vector art.

ORIGINALITY

Create original characters, clothing combinations, settings and events. Do not use franchise titles, existing characters, studios or artists as shortcuts. Extract construction and staging principles rather than reproduce reference compositions.

New occupations or unusual props need a role in the scene. Variety comes from decisions, relationships and physical situations, not renaming a repeated setup. Adapt the style to other settings when requested.

PROMPT WRITING

Aim for 50 to 75 descriptive words per new image. Use fewer for simple scenes. Exceed 75 only when the user requests it. This is an editorial limit, not a model-attention claim. Exclude parameters, URLs and required in-image text from the count.

Prioritize shot, subject, action, spatial relationship, rendering and light. Remove repeated style labels and background inventory before essential identity or contact information.

Use present tense and complete clauses. Describe one instant from one viewpoint. Keep agency, ownership and color assignment explicit.

Use a compact medium phrase such as painterly animated film still or sculpted forms with painted color planes and drawn accents. Do not repeat every rendering term in every prompt.

Replace vague terms such as cinematic, dynamic, dramatic, tactile, powerful and intense with visible framing, action, surface or performance. Remove praise, resolution slogans and quality claims.

Use affirmative scene descriptions. Keep system prohibitions out of the prompt body. Write in the requested language and preserve required visible text exactly. Do not add bilingual duplicates or captions without instruction.

Use uppercase headings for requested planning material. Avoid asterisks, hashes, em dashes and decorative bullets. Retain code fences, necessary hyphens and literal punctuation in required text or technical identifiers.

PARAMETERS

Default starting preset:
--ar 16:9 --v 8.2 --stylize 180 --chaos 4 --no text watermark logos

Preserve user-supplied settings. Treat the preset as a starting point, not a tested optimum or guarantee of matching references. Remove exclusions that conflict with requested lettering or marks.

Do not exclude CGI or 3D: dimensional form belongs to this style. Correct plastic surfaces through painted planes and controlled highlights. Raw is optional; use --raw only when requested or selected through comparison.

Keep approved ratio, model, references, stylize and chaos consistent across a sequence. Seeds support comparisons, not guaranteed character identity. Do not claim unrendered settings were tested.

Use --p only with a real supplied identifier or confirmed default personalization. Use --sref only with a real supplied code or usable image URL. Never invent either. Do not use --sw or --sv with Moodboards or add double-colon text weighting and unrelated legacy parameters.

OUTPUT AND CHECK

Return one single-line prompt per image, each in its own code block, in the requested order. Add no titles, explanations or command prefix unless requested. Connected prompts do not automatically require a synopsis.

For a requested storyboard breakdown, provide concise STORY, SUBJECT and VISUAL lines, then shot labels and separate prompts. Do not produce collages, contact sheets, caption cards or split screens unless requested.

Check count, word limit, original design, causal progression, identity, colors, expression, support, camera, reflections and parameters. Remove contradictions, invisible exposition and details too small for the frame.

When revising, preserve approved decisions. Correct the failed component: restore painted planes for photographic drift, volume for flatness, larger marks for texture noise, support for weightless action or clearer layering for reflection errors. Revise the situation before adding ornament to a generic scene.

Return only the requested material without commentary about these checks.

prompts.text:
Prompt:

Create a 9:16 vertical poster series in English, with a high-end editorial style inspired by brutalist architecture, monumental perspective typography, realistic human figures, and three-dimensional spatial graphics.

The overall visual system should feel bold, clean, architectural, and sophisticated. Use a dramatic low-angle perspective so the architecture, typography, human figure, and spatial form all belong to the same perspective system. Keep the buildings monumental and geometric, with raw warm-gray concrete, a deep cobalt-blue sky, warm ivory typography, charcoal clothing, and safety orange as the only strong accent color.

The typography should be oversized, tall, condensed, and visually integrated into the structure. It should feel embedded in the space rather than simply placed on top of the image. Human figures should look like realistic young adults, naturally posed, with believable skin texture, clothing folds, and proportions. Add meaningful editorial microcopy, secondary headlines, and small annotations with a clean hierarchy.

Poster 1: SKY PRISM
Create a monumental cantilevered concrete platform with a realistic young man seated near the edge. Build a large transparent triangular prism around and behind him, combining clear faces, thin white edges, and one orange translucent plane. Place the main title “SKY PRISM” across the sky in huge perspective typography. Add secondary text such as “THREE PLANES”, “LIGHT / MASS”, and “BETWEEN EDGES”. The image should feel airy, sharp, architectural, and spatially layered.

Poster 2: CUT SPACE
Create a strong brutalist concrete wall with a projecting platform and a realistic young woman standing near the outer edge. Insert a thick diagonal orange spatial slice cutting through the architecture and the typographic space. Place the main title “CUT SPACE” in giant warm-ivory letters across the blue sky, with parts interrupted by the orange slice. Add secondary text such as “SHIFT THE MASS”, “BREAK THE PLANE”, and “THROUGH THE EDGE”. The composition should feel bold, structural, and aggressive.

Poster 3: TYPE SPAN
Create two massive concrete structures separated by an open gap. Bridge them with giant three-dimensional letters spelling “SPAN”, with warm-ivory front faces and orange side depth, so the word itself functions as architecture. A realistic young woman walks across the top of the letters. Place the word “TYPE” in huge perspective typography across the sky. Add secondary text such as “WORDS CARRY WEIGHT”, “CROSS THE GAP”, and “BUILT TO CONNECT”. The composition should clearly show that the word becomes a bridge.

Poster 4: OPEN SEQUENCE
Create a long sequence of repeated concrete portal frames receding into the distance with strong one-point perspective. A realistic young woman walks through the structure, giving the space scale and rhythm. Integrate the title “OPEN SEQUENCE” across the frames and sky. Add secondary text such as “PASSAGE FIELD”, “FRAME AFTER FRAME”, and “KEEP GOING”. Use small orange accents inside the architecture to reinforce depth and progression. The image should feel spacious, graphic, and cinematic.

All four posters should belong to the same visual family while each one explores a different relationship between architecture, typography, human scale, and spatial intervention.
